ID: UQ-20261015-14
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): STEM — indoor-air science / ventilation engineering; neighbours in aerosol-transmission modelling, eDNA methodology, forensic genetics, indoor microbiome.

Question (canonical): In occupied rooms with occupant number, activity (quiet breathing / speech / light exercise) and recirculating HEPA filtration under control and air-exchange rate measured by tracer decay: (a) is R = (size-resolved airborne human-DNA copies per m3, reported separately for an oral/respiratory-marked and a skin-marked fraction) / (CO2-derived rebreathed-air fraction) invariant to occupant number within a pre-registered equivalence band, as any per-occupant-normalised tracer must be; and (b) does R fall under HEPA filtration and shift across particle-size cuts as a particle-borne tracer must and a gas tracer cannot, with the oral/respiratory-marked fraction responding differently from the skin-marked fraction? Third closed outcome: sampling recovery and between-person shedding variance exceed the filtration and activity contrasts.

Alternative formulations:
- Is airborne human DNA a quantitative tracer of shared-breath exposure, and where does it diverge from CO2?
- Can a measured human-DNA-to-CO2 ratio quantify the gas-versus-particle discrepancy that CO2-based infection-risk models assume away?
(Intake wording V0 superseded at Gate 1 for carrying no decision rule; one reformulation used, none remaining.)

Motivating gap: CO2-based rebreathed-air models (Rudnick & Milton 2003) underpin ventilation guidance, but CO2 is a gas tracer untouched by filtration, deposition and size-dependent loss — the terms that dominate particle exposure. Quantitative recovery of human airborne eDNA became routine only ~2021-2023, supplying a human-origin particle-borne tracer. The eDNA and rebreathed-air vocabularies returned disjoint literatures with nothing joining them.

Presuppositions: (1) airborne human DNA is quantitative, not merely detectable — CONTESTED (recovery, qPCR calibration, LOQ; air medians ~0.1 ng, an order below dust); (2) shed human DNA reaches air on particles overlapping respiratory aerosol, requiring an oral/respiratory-versus-skin source marking — CONTESTED, and the record states the partition has no validated assay (oral-microbiome markers are not human DNA; mitochondrial vs nuclear human DNA does not separate oral from skin); (3) CO2 gives a well-defined rebreathed-air fraction — established with documented point-measurement uncertainty; (4) occupancy, activity and ventilation rate independently measurable — established; (5) per-person shedding stable enough for per-occupant normalisation — CONTESTED (analogous viral-load variance spanned orders of magnitude and defeated Kappelt et al.'s own CO2 conversion); (6) collecting human DNA from occupied rooms is ethically/legally admissible — FLAGGED (consent, privacy, surveillance).

What would count as an answer: chamber plus field runs with known occupancy, tracer-decay ventilation, controlled activity, HEPA on/off, size-resolved sampling, assay blanks and spike-recovery, and a per-person shedding-variance estimate from repeat single-occupant runs. YES: R insensitive to occupant number inside pre-registered bands, falling under filtration and shifting across size cuts outside them, oral-marked fraction responding differently from skin-marked. NO: R constant across filtration, activity and size inside the bands — human DNA adds nothing to CO2 and the line closes. NOT QUANTIFIABLE (also closed): pooled recovery plus between-person variance exceed the contrasts. Bands must be fixed from pilot variance that does not yet exist.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 14 web searches across five vocabularies (full list: batches/2026-10-15-1833/UQ-20261015-14-record.md, Gate 2 section), ledger duplicate check over 10 prior entries found no near-duplicate. Most informative: "airborne human DNA indoor air tracer rebreathed air fraction CO2" → only CO2-based risk and rebreathed-air material, no human-DNA tracer; "SARS-CoV-2 RNA air sampling compared with CO2 concentration same rooms exposure surrogate" → Kappelt et al. 2021, the closest prior in the run; "bioaerosol emission rate per occupant normalised to CO2 concentration ratio indoor classroom" → per-occupant emission rates exist, no per-CO2 normalisation; "'shared air' exposure tracer alternative to CO2 biological particle marker ASHRAE" → alternatives discussed are physical/chemical, never biological; "human mitochondrial DNA qPCR air samples indoor occupants HEPA filtration" → no filtration-contrast DNA study. Answer-directed queries were 3, 7, 8, 10, 14. Budget exhausted at 14/14; Bhangar et al. 2014 full text and Thuresson et al. 2024 not opened.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. Kappelt, Russell, Kwiatkowski, Afshari & Johnson, "Correlation of respiratory aerosols and metabolic carbon dioxide", Sustainability 13(21):12203, 2021, doi 10.3390/su132112203 — simultaneous respiratory-aerosol and CO2 measurement, 2 m3 chamber, breathing vs talking; CO2 estimates released particle number but not viral copies.
P2. Whitmore et al., "Inadvertent human genomic bycatch and intentional capture...", Nature Ecology & Evolution 7:873-888, 2023 — species-specific qPCR of human eDNA including occupied vs unoccupied room air, plus consent/surveillance treatment.
P3. Qian, Hospodsky, Yamamoto, Nazaroff & Peccia, "Size-resolved emission rates of airborne bacteria and fungi in an occupied classroom", Indoor Air 22(4):339-351, 2012, PMC3437488 — size-resolved qPCR genome copies, per-occupant emission rates, CO2 used only as a ventilation instrument.
(Further neighbours opened: Adams et al. 2015 PLoS ONE 10(5):e0128022; Fantinato et al. 2023 Sci Rep 13:19059.) Adversary #1 could verify none of these — all its fetches were refused — so no prior here is adversary-confirmed.

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1, the candidate's tracer is human-origin by construction and source-split, varies filtration and particle size (P1 varied neither), tests invariance to occupant number in occupied rooms rather than single-person chamber accumulation, and makes shedding variance a measured parameter with a closed outcome. vs P2, P2's room-air contrast is binary presence with no ventilation rate, CO2, activity, filtration or size resolution, and frames the material as bycatch, not dose. vs P3, P3 has size-resolved qPCR, per-occupant rates and CO2 in one classroom but forms no ratio, targets bacterial/fungal rRNA genes rather than human DNA, and has no filtration contrast.

Novelty confidence: Medium (as recorded at Gate 2; not independently re-tested, since the adversary's Disguise sweep did not execute).

Significance — consequence: YES gives ventilation practice a human-origin, particle-phase exposure index and an empirical check on filtration (equivalent-clean-air) credit without tracer release, and converts the gas-versus-particle discrepancy in Rudnick-Milton-type models into a measured quantity. NO establishes CO2 sufficiency for shared-air indexing and that air DNA is skin/resuspension-dominated, closing an eDNA development line and supporting the forensic presence-not-breathing reading. NOT QUANTIFIABLE bounds forensic occupancy-intensity claims and tells ethics reviewers the surveillance-grade quantitative use is not currently achievable.

Significance — audience: ASHRAE (SSPC 62.1, Standard 241) and REHVA committees deciding whether to add a verification method; hospital infection control running air qPCR with a numerator and no denominator; aerosol-transmission modellers who would replace assumed loss terms; eDNA and forensic method developers; ethics and privacy reviewers.

Significance — fecundity: release-free field measurement of equivalent clean air delivery; whether an oral-marked fraction could index a room's "talking dose"; whether between-person shedding variance sets a floor on any personal-exposure eDNA metric; retrospective reading of archived HVAC filters; behaviour of R under displacement versus mixing ventilation. On NO or NOT QUANTIFIABLE: the resuspended-versus-freshly-shed fraction and its implications for forensic air-DNA interpretation.

Significance — anchoring: tracer-gas versus aerosol-particle divergence indoors; point-measurement uncertainty of CO2 for exposure prediction; unresolved skin-versus-oral source apportionment of indoor human bioaerosol; the human-genetic-bycatch consent debate; forensic air-DNA interpretation and laboratory contamination.

Reason for silence: a disciplinary boundary at the outcome variable — forensic geneticists and eDNA ecologists report identification units (nanograms, profiles, presence/absence), ventilation engineers stop their biology at bacterial and fungal rRNA genes and keep CO2 in the methods section; P3 is a documented near-miss with both quantities in one paper and no ratio formed. Reinforcing: new instrument (routine quantitative human airborne eDNA post-2021) and an incentive/taboo gap around consented human-DNA sampling of classrooms and wards. Adversary #1 raised an unaddressed deflationary rival (silence because practitioners judged the quantitative version visibly defeated by the numbers the record itself cites), which is not an acceptable mechanism and would undercut significance.

Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status) — Adversary #1, verbatim log at UQ-20261015-14-adversary-1.md:
1 | Triviality | Direction of both branches is forced by construction — N cancels in a per-occupant ratio, and DNA is not a gas so R must fall under HEPA; the canonical wording concedes it ("as any per-occupant-normalised tracer must", "as a particle-borne tracer must") | Magnitudes, size-cut profile, oral-vs-skin contrast and whether any exceeds assay noise remain open | Partial
2 | Disguise | Not tested: 0 of the 8 required new-vocabulary queries ran; every WebSearch and WebFetch call was refused for the rest of the session. Three high-risk vocabularies untried by either party — livestock-housing CO2-balance ventilation science, 1960s-80s surgical "air hygiene", wastewater-style human-biomarker (PMMoV/crAssphage) normalisation — plus the two documents the record itself nominated as first Disguise targets | None available | Unresolved (untested by default, explicitly not passed)
3 | Combinatorial novelty | eDNA x ventilation engineering where the interface is already served by cheaper physical particle tracers (P1, ASHRAE 241); the human label only buys background discrimination, which is free in the chamber arm, so it earns its keep only in field rooms where the assay is weakest | Field backgrounds are not subtractable and the oral-vs-skin partition has no physical-particle analogue | Partial
4 | Presupposition failure | The canonical estimand is defined by an oral/respiratory-versus-skin partition that the record itself calls "an unsolved assay-design problem, not a settled technique" while saying it "carries the main inference" — a question naming a measurement that cannot currently be made is under-specified, not hard. Two-sided and untestable without search: if no discriminator exists, part of the question is undefined; if forensic DNA-methylation or host-mRNA body-fluid deconvolution supplies one, the record's flat "unsolved" is wrong and Gate 2 missed a whole vocabulary that may hold priors | The record names the defect and caps itself at Provisional; one could call the partition a downstream engineering sub-problem | Unresolved — the partition sits inside the canonical estimand, not downstream of it
5 | Vagueness | The decision rule is an equivalence band the record admits cannot be set; a band chosen after seeing data does all the work | Fixing bands from pilot variance pre-confirmation is standard, and the explicit third outcome blocks the never-answerable failure mode | Partial
6 | Significance inflation | The flagship audience is least likely to act: ASHRAE/REHVA already accept particle-decay and CADR measurement for filtration credit — cheaper, release-free, no ethics review, no sub-nanogram limit; hospital numerators can be normalised to CO2 or logged occupancy | Surviving audiences (eDNA/forensic method developers, ethics reviewers) are real, and 2/3 already discounts | Partial
7 | Reason for silence | A deflationary rival goes unaddressed: the question may be unasked because it was judged not worth asking, which is not an acceptable mechanism and cuts significance | P3's near-miss is real evidence for a boundary mechanism, and no written dismissal was found | Partial — "none found" is weak when the search that would find one could not run
8 | Dissolution | Decomposes into known physics plus source apportionment: exhaled oral DNA rides the same air as the CO2, so R is constant there up to differential loss, while skin DNA was never in exhaled air and indexes occupancy, not rebreathed air | Mixing proportions are empirical and the experiment delivers the decomposition | Partial

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3

Verdict reasoning (Gate 4, confirmed at Gate 5): Rejected. Attack 4 is Unresolved from Adversary #1 and is fatal under the Gate 4 rule — the canonical question's estimand is constituted by a source partition the record states has no validated assay, so the question as worded names a quantity that cannot currently be measured; this is a defect in the formulation, not a scoring deduction, and it would survive any amount of further searching. Attack 2 is independently Unresolved and also fatal: 0 of the required 8 Disguise queries ran, so Disguise counts as unverified and this entry could not have been Validated on this record whatever else held — three plausible prior-bearing vocabularies (livestock CO2-balance ventilation, surgical air hygiene, wastewater human-biomarker normalisation) and the two documents the record flagged as its own weakest points remain unsearched. Independently, well-posedness is 2/3, below the 3/3 Validated requires. No attack returned Resolved; no prior was adversary-verified. Not routed: the rejection is for presupposition failure and unverified disguise, not for being asked-but-still-open. The record's own note that the sub-question "is airborne human eDNA quantitative" is asked and open as an eDNA methods problem is context, not this candidate.

Strongest remaining objection: the question's estimand is defined by an oral/respiratory-versus-skin human-DNA partition for which no validated assay exists on the record's own account, so part of what is being asked is not yet a measurable quantity (attack 4).

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): before any re-attempt, establish whether forensic tissue-of-origin methods (DNA-methylation or host-mRNA body-fluid deconvolution) can mark oral/respiratory versus skin human DNA at air-sample input masses — and run the unexecuted Disguise sweep in the three untried vocabularies first, since either outcome bears on novelty as much as on feasibility.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): none — not rejected as already-asked.

ID: UQ-20261015-15
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Biology / enzymology and biochemical data curation; AI for science (kcat/KM prediction); neighbours: systems biology (enzyme-constrained GEMs), protein-expression methodology, research-reproducibility meta-science
Question (canonical): Restricted to published kinetic measurement pairs on the same enzyme (same organism, same sequence region, same mutational state) and same substrate that differ only in affinity-tag status (untagged vs tagged, or N- vs C-terminal) and are condition-matched on temperature, pH, buffer and co-substrate saturation: (a) is the pooled within-pair shift in log10 kcat and log10 KM different from zero and direction-consistent, estimated in a mixed model with tag-type, terminus and laboratory terms; and (b) when a published turnover-number predictor (DLKcat, TurNuP, CatPred or RealKcat) is refitted on re-extracted values with versus without tag/terminus stratification, do held-out error and top-k rankings change beyond resampling noise? [R1, adopted at Gate 1; V0 intake version and the reason for reformulation in the record]
Alternative formulations: (1) Is the affinity tag a measurable systematic bias in the enzyme-kinetics literature, or does it only add noise? (2) Do ML kcat predictors trained on tag-unaware databases inherit a construct artefact, and does tag-stratified refitting move their held-out error or top-k predictions?
Motivating gap: Tag effects are documented only per protein and end in "assess case by case" (Majorek 2014; AdSS 2024; staphylokinase 2025). The corpus-level question is absent exactly where it would surface: RealKcat (bioRxiv 2025.02.10.637555) re-read 2,158 articles and resolved 1,804 discrepancies while never using "tag", "affinity tag", "fusion", "terminus" or "purification" (PDF verified in-run, twice); Chen & Nielsen 2021 (PNAS) attribute the heterologous-expression in vitro/in vivo gap to missing PTMs without raising tags. STRENDA Level 1A mandates disclosure of the modification; no kinetics database exposes it as a field (SABIO-RK's queryable vocabulary verified: EnzymeType and IsRecombinant only).
Presuppositions: P1 tag/terminus recoverable at scale - CONTESTED, and partly falsified in the question's favour (BRENDA's Cloned (Commentary) is a displayed, sortable column naming tag status in 10/42 entries of one sampled EC). P2 enough condition-matched pairs exist - CONTESTED and uncounted (principal risk). P3 conditions matchable - CONTESTED (buffer can interact with the exposure: HEPES and uncleaved tag share a site). P4 publication/construct selection tag-independent - CONTESTED (censoring of bad constructs). P5 database values faithful to sources - PARTLY FALSE (1,804 RealKcat corrections; re-extraction required). P6 tag separable from its purification route - CONTESTED; bundle adopted as declared estimand. P7 effect large against predictor error - CONTESTED and adverse. Full statements in the record.
What would count as an answer: a full-text-extracted paired dataset with the pair inventory reported first as a feasibility result; within-pair log-ratio mixed-model estimates with CIs for kcat and KM; then one predictor refitted with and without tag/terminus strata on identically re-extracted labels, against a resampling null. Pre-registered bands: YES-bias = pooled |delta log10| >= 0.2, CI excluding zero, same sign in >= 2 tag classes, and refitting moves error or top-k; NO = both CIs inside +/-0.1 and refitting unchanged (licenses tag-blind pooling); NOISE-NOT-BIAS = CI spans zero with within-pair variance >= between-enzyme variance (weight rather than correct); (a) YES with (b) NO is a fourth closed outcome.
Novelty - queries run (query -> one-line result): 14 distinct queries, 10 fetch attempts with 7 pages opened; full list in batches/2026-10-15-1833/UQ-20261015-15-record.md. Significance - consequence: (a) YES and direction-consistent makes construct metadata a correction term and a candidate database field (standard without schema: STRENDA mandates the disclosure, no kinetics database holds it), and makes tag-blind pooling a known-biased operation. NOISE-NOT-BIAS makes it a weighting variable - a cheaper, different intervention. NO inside the band positively licenses current practice and recasts the case reports as idiosyncratic exceptions. (b) decides whether predictor builders act; (a) YES with (b) NO means a real artefact below current model resolution, bearing on curators and on enzyme-constrained GEMs (which take maximum or selected kcat, where directional bias does not average out) rather than on benchmarks.
Significance - audience: BRENDA and SABIO-RK curators (new field, extraction rule); the STRENDA/Beilstein committee (Level 1A compliance, migration into schemas); kcat/KM predictor groups (RealKcat team cheapest, mid-re-curation of 2,158 articles); enzyme-constrained GEM builders; enzyme-engineering groups ranking variants against literature baselines. ID: UQ-20261015-16
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): STEM — materials chemistry / autonomous experimentation (self-driving labs); neighbours: powder-diffraction crystallography, metrology of automated decision systems (MRMC diagnostic accuracy, calibration/selective prediction).
Question (canonical): For a closed-loop autonomous inorganic-synthesis campaign whose raw diffraction patterns and per-sample automated decision scores are archived (e.g. A-Lab, Szymanski et al. 2023), taking as reference standard the majority verdict of >=3 crystallographers who each classify every pattern as target phase present / absent / indeterminate against a pre-specified minor-phase weight-fraction threshold, blinded to the automated verdict, to one another and to the published per-target conclusion — (a) what is the automated-vs-expert-majority disagreement rate, with CI, over *all* attempted targets (not only reported successes), reported against the measured expert-expert agreement (Fleiss kappa / Gwet AC1) on the same patterns as a noise floor; and (b) is the loop's own deployed phase-identification score calibrated against that blinded majority (pre-specified calibration-slope, Brier and AUC bands) well enough for a running campaign to estimate its own false-discovery rate on-line? Scope: phase identification only; novelty adjudication excluded. (R1, the one permitted Gate-1 reformulation; V0 in the record.)
Alternative formulations:
1. Lay: can a robot lab measure its own error rate — does the match score it already computes predict whether an independent crystallographer, handed the identical pattern with the robot's answer hidden, agrees the target was made?
2. Diagnostic-accuracy: treat the loop as a test and a blinded >=3-reader majority as reference standard; estimate sensitivity, specificity and FDR for the "target synthesized" call, decompose reader-vs-loop against reader-vs-reader variance (MRMC), and test the score for calibration.
3. Dependence: does automated-vs-expert disagreement on identical campaign data scale with fitted-phase count, amorphous fraction, SNR, or target structural prototype?
Motivating gap: The same A-Lab diffraction data have produced two incompatible readings in print — Leeman/Palgrave et al. (PRX Energy 3:011002, 2024): no new materials, ~2/3 of claimed successes likely known disordered analogues; Nature Author Correction (650(8100):E1, 19 Jan 2026): the platform "reached the correct conclusion in 36 of its 40 reported successes", 4 inconclusive from XRD alone, novelty reframed as "new to the prediction platform". Neither is a measurement: both unblinded, by interested parties, on reported successes only, no CI, no second independent reader, no expert-expert baseline, nothing on the loop's internal score. Success counts from such loops are cited by funders and reviewers with no error bar.
Presuppositions: (1) campaigns retain raw patterns AND per-sample decision scores — established for A-Lab patterns, NOT established for scores on failed targets (both adversaries failed to confirm; feasibility gate for (b)); (2) a blinded expert majority can serve as reference standard — contested by design, hence the in-study kappa noise floor; (3) "target present" is a definable binary near the detection limit — contested; handled by pre-specified weight-fraction threshold + indeterminate category + sensitivity thresholds; (4) scores comparable across samples — untested; if within-target only, (b) becomes a rank statistic; (5) automated and expert verdicts address the same proposition — claimed resolved by scoping to phase ID, but adversary 2 notes the scoping may remove most of the published disagreement; (6) a control subset with independent ground truth is obtainable — flagged feasibility risk; (7) NOT presupposed that the loop is wrong.
What would count as an answer: a pre-registered blinded re-read of an existing campaign archive (all released A-Lab patterns, all 58 attempted targets, or a comparable campaign): >=3 independent readers, present/absent/indeterminate + confidence, randomised order, replicate subset for intra-reader agreement; (a) disagreement rate with CI over all targets (so sensitivity/specificity/FDR are estimable) beside measured Fleiss kappa / Gwet AC1 and MRMC variance decomposition; (b) reliability curve, calibration slope/intercept, Brier, AUC for the deployed score against the blinded majority with pre-specified bands, plus implied vs realised on-line FDR; (c) regression of disagreement on phase count, amorphous fraction, SNR, prototype; control subset to bound reference-standard error. Three closed outcomes: calibrated (campaign can self-estimate FDR); flat/inverted (external human audit required); disagreement inside the expert-expert noise floor (the binary call is undefined at the detection limit for humans too — report weight fractions with uncertainty and retire the success count).
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 Gate-2 searches + 5 fetches; 8 disguise searches + 4 fetches (adversary 1); 11 disguise searches + 4 fetches (adversary 2) — 30 queries, 13 pages opened, all vocabularies distinct. Full lists: batches/2026-10-15-2033/UQ-20261015-16-record.md, UQ-20261015-16-adversary-1.md, UQ-20261015-16-adversary-2.md. Most informative: `A-Lab response critique Szymanski Ceder reply 2024 rebuttal` → the Nature Author Correction (decisive hit); `machine learning XRD phase identification uncertainty quantification calibration reliability diagram Brier` → CrystalShift (calibration against simulated ground truth); `"inter-annotator agreement" powder diffraction phase labels expert annotators XRD` (adv. 1) → Hattrick-Simpers et al. 2021 NIST consensus human+ML XRD labels with quantified uncertainty — missed by Gate 2, the single most damaging hit of the run; `Reynolds Cup participants misidentified phases qualitative identification errors` (adv. 1) → Raven & Self 2017, 448 participants, documented missed/misidentified phases; `fraction of robotic laboratory discovery claims confirmed by independent reanalysis measured error rate 2026` (adv. 2) → Trustworthy Autonomous Science roadmap (arXiv:2607.12113), demands checks "against independent measurements the agent does not control", reports no agreement rate; IUCr CPD QPA round robin (opened, adv. 2) → on identical data a 31.37 wt% phase returned over 22.40–48.60 wt%, a 1.15 wt% phase returned as 0.00 — large same-data analyst scatter, but no identification-agreement statistic. No query in any vocabulary returned a blinded multi-reader agreement rate against a noise floor, or a calibration of a deployed loop's own score.

P1 — Author Correction to "An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of inorganic materials", Nature 650(8100):E1, 19 Jan 2026, doi:10.1038/s41586-025-09992-y (opened and independently verified by both adversaries): builders' manual re-read, 36/40 correct, 4 inconclusive.

Mater. Manuf. Innov. 2021 (dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/136823): multi-expert consensus XRD phase labels, label variance quantified by Shannon entropy, used as the benchmark for ML phase labels; expert count unstated, no kappa, blinding not stated. Runner-up P4 — Dara, arXiv:2510.19667: n=1 unblinded expert on 20 A-Lab patterns, no agreement statistic.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — dispute resolution, not measurement: one interested unblinded team, reported successes only (so no specificity, no FDR, no missed successes among the 17–18 failures), bare count with no CI, no second reader, no noise floor, nothing on the internal score, so (b) untouched; P2's incompatible reading of identical data is itself the evidence that one unblinded re-read does not settle the quantity. vs P2 — same deficits, opposite conclusion, and its verdicts are substantially about novelty/cation disorder rather than phase presence. vs P3 — calibration already asked and answered for a candidate algorithm against synthetic labels; candidate differs in reference standard (blinded multi-expert majority on real campaign patterns), object (the score a deployed loop actually used), target quantity (campaign-level on-line FDR vs realised FDR), and dependence terms. vs P0 — P0 is the closest prior to part (a) and the reason this entry cannot be Validated: the generic move "measure expert label disagreement on XRD patterns, then score machine labels against it" is already asked and answered. The candidate differs by corpus (a closed-loop campaign archive, including declared failures), by method (blinding, >=3 independent readers, kappa/AC1 and intra-reader agreement, pre-specified weight-fraction threshold, MRMC decomposition) and by object (a deployed decision score and a campaign FDR, not a research model's labels) — but "corpus + method upgrade on an asked question" is exactly the pattern the ledger rejects, and only (b) plus the FDR link stands clear of it.
Novelty confidence: Medium
(Judge's note, binding: Medium is for the conjunction (a)+(b) only, and is the lowest defensible reading of it. Part (a) taken alone is Low — P0 asks it generically, P1/P2 ask the coarse A-Lab version in print, and the Reynolds Cup / IUCr CPD literature has documented analyst misidentification for two decades. Part (b) — calibration of a deployed loop's own score against a blinded expert majority, converted into an on-line campaign FDR — was returned by no query in 30 across 10+ vocabularies, including forensic black-box, Eurachem/IUPAC qualitative-method validation, JCGM-106 conformity assessment, metabolomics decoy FDR, automated mineralogy, XPS inter-analyst audits, German Ringversuch, Chinese, and SDPD round robins. The Gate-2 search record is also incomplete as written: it missed P0, the Reynolds Cup and the 2026 roadmap, which independently bars Validated.)
Significance — consequence: If calibrated — a campaign converts a number it already computes into a running FDR estimate, success counts acquire a self-generated error bar, score-thresholded triage of which samples need human reading becomes defensible. If flat/inverted — the internal score is not evidence about correctness, self-reported success counts cannot be audited from inside the loop, evidence standards must require external reading of a random sample (the disagreement rate sets the sample size), and headline-count platform comparisons become uninterpretable. If inside the noise floor — the binary is undefined at the detection limit for humans too, so the field should report refined weight fractions with uncertainty and retire the success-count metric.
Significance — audience: Demonstrated, not asserted: Nature issued a correction on exactly this axis; the builders responded by building Dara with an expert comparison (n=1, unblinded), i.e. they are already reaching for the measurement; the critics published in a journal; and a 2026 community roadmap (arXiv:2607.12113, opened by adversary 2) cites this correction, notes automated refinement "below the quality a human expert would accept", and asks for checks "against independent measurements that the agent does not control" while having no such measurement to point at. Beyond those: DOE/ARPA-E/EU materials-acceleration funders, Acceleration Consortium, Argonne Polybot, IUCr CPD.
Significance — fecundity: cheapest audit design (readers x sampling fraction) bounding campaign FDR to a stated width — unposable before the noise floor is known; transfer of the protocol to other automated readouts gating autonomous claims (NMR structure verification, cryo-EM map interpretation, LLM-as-judge screens) as decision-level metrology for SDLs; binding conformal/selective prediction to an expert reference standard rather than synthetic labels; whether disagreement concentrates in identifiable prototypes or disordered systems, so pipelines can avoid targets their own verification cannot adjudicate; whether "weight fraction with uncertainty" should replace binary success as the reporting unit.
Significance — anchoring: the A-Lab dispute and its correction; the ordered-vs-disordered-compound reproducibility problem; the IUCr CPD / Reynolds Cup between-analyst variability tradition (now cited, not merely flagged); blind testing of automated structure determination (CASD-NMR, SDPD round robins) as the precedent for auditing automation by withholding the answer; UQ for ML phase labelling (P3, P0).
Reason for silence: Incentive gap plus data recency, credible: no party gains from running it — builders would publish their own error rate (cheaper move, demonstrated: build a better tool and compare against one cooperating expert), critics gain more from case-by-case refutation than from a rate that may come out reassuring, and the correction process rewards settling these compounds rather than the general quantity; the "same data, two independent readings" corpus only existed after the 2024 dispute forced pattern release. The record's first mechanism (crystallography has no tradition of treating a human reading as a fallible rater) is STRUCK by adversary 1's P0 and the Reynolds Cup: that tradition exists. Adversary 2 substitutes a weaker conceptual-bridge mechanism — a community document devoted to trustworthy autonomous science reaches for this concern and lands on "independent measurements" and generic UQ, never on an agreement rate, a noise floor or a calibration curve, i.e. it lacks the vocabulary to formulate the ask. Accepted as a partial account only.

ID: UQ-20261015-17
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): STEM — atmospheric science / numerical weather prediction; AI (data-driven forecast models). Neighbours: data assimilation (observation influence / DFS), forecast verification science.
Question (canonical): For a fixed period and forecast set, both model families started from the same operational analysis and scored under one pre-specified metric set (RMSE, bias, CRPS, an extreme-event score) per variable/level/region: does the data-driven-minus-physical skill difference measured against the analysis/reanalysis the data-driven models were trained on (Delta_analysis) equal, within a pre-specified equivalence band, the same difference measured against observations that did not inform that analysis there and then (blacklisted, post-cutoff, unassimilated networks, or withheld in an OSE) (Delta_obs) — and does Delta_analysis − Delta_obs scale with a per-location/level/variable measure of how weakly the analysis is constrained by observations (observation influence, DFS, analysis-ensemble spread)?
Alternative formulations:
- (V0, intake) For identical forecast sets, is the AI-vs-physical skill gap the same scored against the training reanalysis as against independent in-situ observations, and does any discrepancy grow where the analysis is weakly observation-constrained?
- (lay) Do AI weather models look better than the physics model mainly because they are graded against the model-made dataset they were trained on, and most so where there are fewest real observations?
Motivating gap: Inverts the settled claim "data-driven models beat the operational physical model" by questioning its presupposition that analysis-space skill is an unbiased estimate of skill against the atmosphere. Obs-space verification is routine; the record claims the unfound object is the *paired* quantity Delta_analysis − Delta_obs resolved by observational constraint.
Presuppositions: (1) analyses are model-dependent in a quantifiable, spatially/vertically/variable-dependent way — ESTABLISHED (observation-influence/DFS diagnostics; Hu et al. 2025, doi 10.1029/2024MS004809, listing only); (2) observations independent of the analysis and training data exist — CONTESTED IN PRACTICE, hence four enumerated independence routes; (3) observation and representativeness error are tractable enough for an obs-space gap to be interpretable — STANDARD BUT NON-TRIVIAL, explicitly contested for surface/boundary-layer variables and precipitation; (4) both families scorable on the same initial times and lead times — ESTABLISHED, with a shared initial state forced; (5) "skill gap" well defined per variable/level/region under a pre-registered metric set — ESTABLISHED; (6) a per-location/level/variable constraint measure can be joined to verification output — CONTESTED ON ACCESS (computed inside operational DA systems, not published as gridded fields). Not presupposed: the sign or non-zeroness of the discrepancy.
What would count as an answer: a verification study over a fixed period and forecast set computing Delta_analysis and Delta_obs for the same forecasts per variable/level/region, reporting the paired difference with block-bootstrap uncertainty over initial times and regressing it on an observation-influence measure. Presupposition holds if the paired difference stays inside the pre-specified band; fails if exceeded, with sign and constraint slope reported. Third admitted closed outcome: observation and representativeness error make the paired contrast unresolvable at available sample size — itself decision-relevant for verification standards.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 web searches (cap reached), 5 fetches (3 succeeded); full list in batches/2026-10-15-2033/UQ-20261015-17-record.md. Most informative: (1) "AI weather model skill verified against observations instead of ERA5 reanalysis circularity" → arXiv:2305.00048, the near-duplicate, as first hit; (2) "GraphCast Pangu-Weather verification against radiosonde observations observation space scores" → arXiv:2509.01879 plus github.com/ZzZTripleZzZ/castcheck station-level verification; (4) "observation influence degrees of freedom for signal reanalysis model-determined AI weather forecast evaluation data-sparse" → DA-methodology only, no link to AI verification; (6) "ECMWF AIFS verification against observations headline scores same as IFS newsletter observation space" → AIFS GMD 19:4703-4724 (2026), both spaces verified, contrast not taken; (9) "benchmark ground truth generated by a model inflates scores of models trained on it" (ML vocabulary) → LLM self-bias/contamination only; (11) "withheld unassimilated observations observing system experiment evaluate data-driven weather model independent truth" → DABench/OSE literature, no paired AI-vs-physical OSE study. Not read, so not relied on: ScienceDirect review S2950630126000013 (robots-disallowed), WeatherBench 2 JAMES full text (fetch failed).
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): N1. Ramavajjala & Mitra (Excarta), "Verification against in-situ observations for Data-Driven Weather Prediction", arXiv:2305.00048 — FourCastNet vs IFS scored against MADIS 2020 surface observations and against ERA5; against ERA5 the data-driven model wins, against observations "both FCN and IFS perform nearly identically", and reanalysis verification is argued to give DDWPs "an unfair advantage". N2. Gupta, Sheshadri & Suri, "An Observations-focused assessment of Global AI Weather Prediction Models During the South Asian Monsoon", arXiv:2509.01879v1 — seven AI models plus GenCast vs HRES/IFS ENS against 458 IMD stations; errors against stations exceed those against ERA5 by 15-45%. N3. Moldovan, Pinnington, Prieto Nemesio et al., "AIFS Single 1.1.0", Geosci. Model Dev. 19:4703-4724 (2026), doi 10.5194/gmd-19-4703-2026 — verifies in both spaces and states "We verify against the operational IFS analysis, which is also used to initialise the forecasts."
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs N1 — same question and same answer direction; the candidate adds a paired statistic with uncertainty, an observation-influence regression, genuinely unassimilated observations, wider scope, and removal of the initialisation confound. That is a hardened, better-controlled version of N1's question, not a different one. vs N2 — same inversion, many models but regional and near-surface, and it compares error *levels* under two references rather than the AI-minus-physical *gap*; no pairing, no uncertainty, data density discussed only qualitatively. vs N3 — an operational centre that computes both halves of the contrast, names the circularity in passing, and never subtracts them or treats data-sparse regions.
Novelty confidence: Low
Significance — consequence: inside the band, the circularity objection is retired with a number; outside it, every headline comparison acquires a reference-dependent correction whose sign matters either way (AI advantage partly inherited from the training target, or AI under-credited by analysis-space scoring), and a non-zero constraint slope turns the caveat into a map of where analysis-space scores can be trusted. The unresolvable outcome would itself argue for reserved unassimilated reference networks.
Significance — audience: WMO verification bodies (LCDNV, WIPPS) deciding whether obs-space verification becomes mandatory for data-driven systems; national services weighing operational adoption; AI-model developers choosing reference datasets and training targets; downstream procurers (energy, aviation, reinsurance) who buy on the analysis-space number alone; reanalysis producers. Real rather than asserted: all three constituencies have already published on the first clause (N1 commercial, N2 academic, N3 operational).
Significance — fecundity: obs-space loss targeted at steep-slope regions; whether the slope shrinks as training targets move to obs-assimilating/obs-trained analyses (arXiv:2407.15586, 2607.07879); the analogous slope for the physical model against its own analysis; whether the slope predicts which AI failure modes (blurring, under-dispersion, boundary-layer bias) are training-target artefacts; the general question of inherited structure in any learner trained on a model-based product.
Significance — anchoring: the observation-impact/DFS literature (supplies the regressor, currently used only for DA monitoring); the pre-AI verification problem of a model-dependent reference, taught as a caveat with no measured size; the live anomaly of a large analysis-space and small obs-space AI advantage (N1, N2) with competing unseparated causes; the deployment decisions now in front of operational centres (N3).
Reason for silence: not "no one thought of it" — N1 and N3 come within one subtraction. (1) Disciplinary boundary with an asymmetric data holding: the observation-influence regressor lives inside operational DA systems and is not published as a joinable gridded field, so outsiders argue the circularity instead of measuring it. (2) An incentive gradient in the protocol: analysis space yields cheap, uniform, comparable, publishable scores while obs space is sparse, error-laden and network-dependent, and the independence requirement makes it scarcer still; no party's reward function pays for the subtraction or for pre-registering an equivalence band. Both mechanisms are credible for the *second* clause only — the first clause has in fact been asked, which is why the silence story supports "hardening of an asked question" rather than "un-asked".

ID: UQ-20261015-18
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Biology — protein engineering / directed evolution, deep mutational scanning; AI for science (surrogate-guided design). Transplant source: quantitative genetics / breeding. Source method: cross-field transplant.
Question (canonical): In published multi-round protein-engineering campaigns meeting stated inclusion criteria (>=2 replicates per screened variant; screened and carried-forward counts reported; round r+1's library derived from round r's selected variants by mutagenesis, recombination or surrogate-guided sampling in the same neighbourhood; de novo generative redesign excluded), (a) does the realized round-over-round change in library mean trait value, on a pre-registered log/Tobit-censored scale, agree with the breeder's-equation prediction R-hat = i x rho x sigma_g (i from the reported selection fraction with finite-library correction; rho = sqrt of replicate-based variant repeatability for assay-based selection, or surrogate prediction-measurement correlation as indirect-selection accuracy; sigma_g the among-variant SD from round r alone) — reported as calibration slope with 95% CI, mean bias and 80%/95% interval coverage, all inputs from round r only; and (b) at each campaign's own well budget N = n x m, does the predicted-gain-maximizing (n, m) split differ materially (>=20% of per-round gain forgone) from the split the campaign used?
Alternative formulations:
- A1: Is per-round response to selection in directed-evolution and ML-guided design predictable in advance from assay noise, library diversity and selection fraction, as breeders predict genetic gain per cycle?
- A2: At a fixed number of assay wells, are protein campaigns screening too many variants too noisily (or too few too precisely) relative to the gain-maximizing allocation?
(Gate 1 reformulation record, V0 -> R1, in batches/2026-10-15-2033/UQ-20261015-18-record.md.)
Motivating gap: Quantitative genetics has predicted gain per selection cycle, optimal allocation of test capacity between candidates and replication, and selection on a correlated predictor (selection-index accuracy = an ML surrogate) for a century. Protein campaigns instead report hit rates and best-variant fold-improvement; the ML side frames the loop as Bayesian optimization under regret; library-design theory concerns diversity, not predicted gain under a noisy assay.
Presuppositions: (1) >=20 published campaigns retain per-round replicate structure and reported counts — contested, unverified, made an inclusion criterion; (2) phenotype variance decomposes into variant and assay components — established given replicates (Enrich2-style); (3) breeder's-equation assumptions hold within a round, incl. roughly additive variation among the selected variants' descendants — contested, epistasis strong; (4) selection intensity recoverable — criterion, not assumption; (5) a scale on which means/variances compare across rounds — contested, censoring rule stipulated; (6) surrogate rho from round r stands in for accuracy on the selected tail — contested; (7) not presupposed that the theory fits. NOT flagged by the record, and fatal at Gate 4: (8) that a selected variant's measured value is transmitted intact to the library built from it, i.e. transmissibility = 1 — false for the mutagenesis and surrogate-sampling rounds R1 admits.
What would count as an answer: (a) retrospective test over >=20 qualifying campaigns — "yes" = slope CI inside 0.75–1.33 with coverage within 10 points of nominal; "no" = biased prediction with the bias attributed to a named mechanism (sigma_g loss => epistasis; shortfall in surrogate rounds => selection accuracy; shortfall tracking censored share => saturation). (b) per-campaign gain forgone by the actual (n, m) split (<10% small, >=20% material). (c) ideally one pre-registered prospective round, theory-optimal vs default allocation.
Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 13 generator queries across four vocabularies (protein engineering, quantitative genetics/breeding, DMS/benchmarks, BO/ML design), plus 9 new queries per adversary in 7 and 9 further vocabularies respectively (German, Chinese, Price/Robertson identity, I-O-psychology utility analysis, generalizability theory, OR ranking-and-selection/OCBA, historical mutation breeding, phage display, psychometric attenuation). Full lists: batches/2026-10-15-2033/UQ-20261015-18-record.md and the two adversary files. Most informative: "breeder's equation" directed evolution response to selection per round -> no application, returns selection-stringency work only; optimum allocation number of genotypes versus replications maximize selection gain (Longin/Melchinger) -> CRAN selectiongain and TAG papers, i.e. arm (b) is packaged off-the-shelf in breeding; Brogden-Cronbach-Gleser utility equation selection ratio x validity x SDy -> the same product asked in personnel selection, never applied to variant libraries; "Bulmer effect" / loss of genetic variance in protein libraries -> nothing, groundwork absent; attenuation correction / per-assay repeatability as a noise ceiling on ProteinGym -> unclaimed; Chinese and German transplant queries -> the two literatures returned side by side, never joined. No search call was refused; both adversaries completed their >=8 Disguise queries, so Disguise is verified, not unverified.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): 1. Alpay & Desai, "Effects of selection stringency on the outcomes of directed evolution," bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.06.09.598029 (read via par.nsf.gov/10527325; later version 10653062 re-read by adversary 1). 2. Subramanian, "Does Benchmark Correlation Predict Selection Quality for Protein Design?", NeurIPS 2026 workshop, neurips.cc/virtual/2026/178310 (verified real by both adversaries). 3. Dai et al., "Batch Bayesian Optimization for Replicable Experimental Design," arXiv 2311.01195 (verified). Added by adversaries as prior art the record missed: CRAN selectiongain (Cochran 1951; Utz 1969; Tallis 1961; Longin et al. 2007; Mi/Utz/Technow/Melchinger 2014) and the breeding resource-allocation corpus (Genet. Sel. Evol. 10.1186/s12711-019-0491-5, 10.1186/1297-9686-28-1-3; "Optimal Replication in Selection Experiments"); OR ranking-and-selection/OCBA; Brogden-Cronbach-Gleser utility analysis; generalizability-theory D-studies. Also nearby: ACIDES (Nat. Commun. 14:8504); Boyer et al. arXiv 1509.02450; bioRxiv 2025.11.09.687419.
Novelty — how this differs from each: Alpay & Desai vary selection stringency but predict max fitness of the next population, explicitly neglect measurement noise and hold n fixed — no mean response, no repeatability, no (n, m) split. Subramanian audits rank correlation as a proxy for top-k selection value on static assays — no repeatability, library-variance or per-round gain term. Dai et al. state the candidate-vs-replicate tradeoff but as a no-regret algorithm on agriculture/AutoML, never proteins, never breeding theory. Against the adversary-supplied prior art the difference narrows sharply: arm (b) is the Cochran-Utz-Longin optimum with protein numbers substituted (same product also asked in personnel selection and G-theory), so the composite's novelty rests almost entirely on arm (a).
Novelty confidence: Medium
Significance — consequence: If calibrated, per-round gain becomes forecastable and budgetable from two measurable numbers before wells are spent, and assay repeatability becomes reportable the way Z' is. If not, the direction of the miss was claimed to localize to epistasis, surrogate accuracy or censoring; both adversaries find these channels non-identifiable in a retrospective corpus, so that payoff is not secured. A material allocation gap would show money spent on the wrong margin; a small gap would vindicate current practice, which is at present asserted rather than checked.
Significance — audience: Platform and academic groups sizing screens (wells per variant, every round); DMS/MAVE consortia designing replicate structure; benchmark builders (ProteinGym, FLIP, SSMuLA) whose rankings are partly rankings of assay noise; breeders, as a stress test of their own theory under strong epistasis. Judge's discount: both adversaries note the audiences optimize the best variant, not the library mean, and that m is often fixed by assay format and plate layout, so the wells-per-variant action is not demonstrated to be free.
Significance — fecundity: Would make askable whether an effective heritability of a protein assay is a stable reportable property; a persistence-of-variance (Bulmer-analogue) coefficient for libraries; surrogate retraining as an increase in rho rather than a change of acquisition function; rounds-versus-depth as breeding-cycle-time optimization; reconstruction of best-variant improvement from mean plus variance.
Significance — anchoring: Local additivity of fitness landscapes for short-horizon prediction; winner's curse / regression to the mean in screening hits; benchmark validity when correlation decouples from top-k selection value; unused DMS variance decompositions; the Bulmer effect.
Reason for silence: Disciplinary boundary (the breeder's equation is taught in breeding, not biochemistry or ML-for-biology) plus an occupied formalism (BO/regret), a reporting convention that publishes best-variant fold-improvement and discards replicate variance as a QC gate, a weak publication incentive for the prospective arm, and recent-data availability. Adversary 1 rates this Resolved on the reporting-convention leg (evidenced: the nearest prior states its outcome is max fitness and neglects noise). Adversary 2 rates it Partial and offers a more parsimonious competing mechanism the record never tested: that the same formalism is independently asked in four other fields, so it is not venue-bound, and anyone sitting down with both literatures meets the transmissibility misspecification within a page and drops it — silence because the transplant does not work.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): two independent fresh-context adversaries, 9 searches + 4 fetches each; verbatim logs in batches/2026-10-15-2033/UQ-20261015-18-adversary-1.md and -adversary-2.md.

Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — laboratory medicine / clinical chemistry and in-vitro diagnostics; human genetics (biobank–EHR linkage). Neighbours: affinity proteomics (epitope effects), IVDR post-market performance follow-up, measurement-error epidemiology.
Question (canonical): [R1, adopted at Gate 1; full pre-registration text in batches/2026-10-15-2033/UQ-20261015-19-record.md] In biobanks linking whole-genome/exome data to routine clinical laboratory results (UK Biobank primary-care and hospital extracts, All of Us EHR labs, national lab registries), over a pre-registered analyte set fixed by a published feasibility census of resolvable assay/platform metadata: (a) do coding variants in the gene encoding the measured analyte (single-variant plus epitope-agnostic gene-based burden) associate with the immunoassay-reported clinical value, adjusted for a trans PGS, ancestry, age, sex, assay era and site, and replicate in a second biobank; (b) where two or more platforms are recorded, is there a variant-by-platform interaction; (c) in people measured for the same analyte by both immunoassay and a variant-agnostic orthogonal method (LC-MS/MS on peptides not spanning the variant site, or an activity assay), does the genotype effect fall inside a pre-specified equivalence band (assay-bias prediction) or persist outside it (proteoform-physiology prediction); and (d) for each surviving effect, what is the rate of clinical decision-threshold crossings per 100,000 tests among tested carriers, with CIs, and does carriers' downstream care differ? Pre-specified third outcome: if the census finds too few analytes with usable platform metadata, the reportable answer is the bounded feasibility result plus (a) and (d), with (b) declared not estimable.
Alternative formulations:
- What is the population prevalence of clinically misleading laboratory results caused by the patient's own epitope-region variants, assay by assay?
- Which routine immunoassays carry a cis effect of the analyte gene that disappears under a variant-agnostic orthogonal measurement, and how many threshold crossings per 100,000 tests does each cause?
Motivating gap: The join (population-scale genomes + routine clinical lab results + platform metadata) is new; the mechanism is established only case by case (HbA1c in G6PD/Hb-variant carriers, macro-TSH, variant hCG, GDF-15 H202D, and — found at Gate 4 — FDH/ALB R218H across current FT4 methods, F8 one-stage/chromogenic discrepancy, D-variant serologic typing) and, in research affinity proteomics, as cis "epitope effects". No cross-assay, population-scale prevalence or decision-impact estimate exists. Clinical chemistry manages interference through case reports and spiked-interferent testing with no genotype arm; biobank lab-GWAS reads cis signals as biology.
Presuppositions: P1 routine extracts carry enough analyzer/platform metadata to separate assay from biology (contested; itself a reported outcome). P2 a variant-agnostic orthogonal method exists in a subset of the same people at estimable N (contested; Gate 4 finds this asserted, no cohort named). P3 epitopes are mappable (contested; deliberately not relied on — primary test is epitope-agnostic). P4 attenuation under an orthogonal method implies assay bias rather than real proteoform physiology (contested; the central inferential risk). P5 the orthogonal method is itself variant-agnostic (contested; peptide selection pre-specified, activity assays carry the mirror risk). P6 decision thresholds are stable enough to count crossings (largely established). P7 carriers are numerous enough among tested people (contested; gene-based collapsing specified). Not presupposed: that prevalence is high.
What would count as an answer: A ranked list of assays, each with a per-100,000-test misclassification rate and CI, built from a replicated cis coding-variant association on the reported clinical value, a variant-by-platform interaction where platform is recorded, a within-person orthogonal comparison against a stated equivalence band, and threshold crossings plus downstream-care differences in carriers. A bounded null ("fewer than X crossings per 100,000 tests across N testable analytes, 95% upper bound") is equally admissible, as is the pre-specified feasibility census.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 29 distinct queries total (Gate 2: 11; adversary 1: 9 new vocabularies; adversary 2: 9 new vocabularies), plus 13 fetch attempts (2 blocked by reCAPTCHA, 1 lost to a 302). Full lists: batches/2026-10-15-2033/UQ-20261015-19-record.md, -adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md. Most informative: "coding variants in analyte's own gene bias immunoassay results biobank" → epitope-effect preprint + GDF-15, nothing on routine-care prevalence; "genotype-dependent analytical bias, patient misclassification at clinical decision limit, prevalence" → bias treated solely as an instrument property, never a patient property; "how many routine clinical assays affected by patient coding variants ... proportion of immunoassays" (answer-seeking) → no published proportion for clinical assays; "familial dysalbuminemic hyperthyroxinemia ALB R218H method-dependent falsely elevated free T4 which assays" → limbs (b)+(c) executed by hand for one analyte, entity called "underdiagnosed"; "factor VIII one-stage chromogenic assay discrepancy F8 genotype prevalence misclassification" → a named subfield ("assay discrepancy") with dual-assay guidance; "RHD variant serology genotype discordance prevalence" → the structural question as routine audit with published discordance rates; "CST3 cystatin C coding variant immunoassay eGFR bias" → Titan et al. 2026, population-scale genetic bias in a routine analyte, no reclassification count; German and French phrasings → no formulation in either language; "variant-by-assay interaction analyzer platform heterogeneity clinical lab GWAS" → LabWAS only, no platform-interaction study. Disguise searches were executed by both adversaries (9 and 9, each ≥8 new vocabularies), so Disguise is verified as run, not unverified; it returned Partial from both.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): P-A. "Familial dysalbuminaemic hyperthyroxinaemia interferes with current free thyroid hormone immunoassay methods" — Cambridge repository record https://www.repository.cam.ac.uk/handle/1810/303864 (PMC7222281), with "Familial Dysalbuminemic Hyperthyroxinemia: An Underdiagnosed Entity" (PMC7408830); title/repository level only, full text reCAPTCHA-blocked. P-B. "Epitope Effect Prevalence in Affinity-based pQTL studies", bioRxiv 2025.06.20.660695 (opened and independently verified by both adversaries; author block not exposed, so not stated): 34–36% of cis-pQTL proteins carry a missense variant in strong LD; 37 opposing-direction and 85 single-platform discrepancies; concludes epitope effects plausibly affect ≤12% of assayed proteins; no orthogonal measurement. P-C. Pavlova A, Delev D, Pezeshkpoor B, Müller J, Oldenburg J, Thromb Haemost 2014;111(5):851-861 (opened): 23 missense F8 variants indexed by which of two assays reads higher, 99 discrepant patients, authors note failure to diagnose or misclassified severity, dual-assay diagnosis recommended. Adjacent, also real and opened/verified: Wheeler et al., PLoS Med 2017;14(9):e1002383 (G6PD G202A, ~2% of African American adults with T2D missed by HbA1c); GDF-15 H202D (Hyvönen lab page, re-surfaced independently); Titan et al., Kidney Int 2026, doi:10.1016/j.kint.2026.07.018 (UK Biobank non-GFR genetic bias in creatinine/cystatin C, varying by self-reported race, no threshold crossings); LabWAS, medRxiv 2020.04.08.19011478 / PMC7682892 (flagship lab-GWAS design with no analyzer field); Arnoni et al., Immunohematology 2024;40(2):47-53 (D-variant typing discordance rates). Not cited as support: a JAMA 2017 sickle-trait/HbA1c analysis seen only via news coverage.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P-A — same mechanism, same two discriminating limbs, but one analyte, referred patients, no population denominator, no crossing rate, no systematic scan; the candidate asks what P-A-type cells aggregate to across the test menu. vs P-B — research affinity platforms, no patient, no regulated IVD, no clinical threshold, no orthogonal arm; its discriminator is affinity-vs-affinity disagreement plus structural annotation, an upper bound on research assays. vs P-C — two activity assays in already-diagnosed patients, no immunoassay-vs-non-affinity contrast, no population scale, no per-100,000 rate; and it is the clearest evidence that method disagreement can reflect real proteoform behaviour rather than bias.
Novelty confidence: Medium — downgraded at Gate 4 from a clean Medium to Medium-with-a-close-neighbour; both adversaries recommend Medium-Low. Not Low: no source asks or answers the candidate's estimand (cross-assay census, variant-by-platform interaction in linked care data, population-scale variant-agnostic orthogonal arm, crossings per 100,000 tests). Not High or clean Medium: Gate 2 missed three nearer neighbours (P-A, P-C, Titan 2026) and four vocabularies (immunohaematology, thyroid eponyms, nephrology/eGFR, serology/Ig allotype), and the source method is better described as a cross-field transplant than a new-instrument question.
Significance — consequence: If yes for any analyte, a reported clinical number is wrong in a direction fixed by the patient's genome, inherited, and unequally distributed by ancestry — converting a per-case curiosity into a population quantity that justifies or refutes insert warnings, reflex rules and calibrator/epitope redesign by a number instead of anecdote. If no, a tight upper bound licenses what lab-GWAS and cis-MR of immunoassay-measured biomarkers currently assume without test: that the cis signal in the analyte's own gene is biology, not binder failure — an exclusion-restriction violation no MR sensitivity analysis probes. The feasibility-limited outcome names a metadata gap for laboratory data standards.
Significance — audience: IVD manufacturers and notified bodies under IVDR post-market performance follow-up; IFCC/CLSI interference and standardisation committees, whose framework has spiked-interferent arms and no genotype arm; laboratory directors setting reflex, delta-check and orthogonal-confirmation rules, who need no epitope disclosure to act; guideline writers owning the crossed thresholds, with documented responsiveness to this evidence class (HbA1c/G6PD guidance, method-specific FT4 advice around FDH, RHD genotyping policy); biobank custodians and lab-GWAS/MR groups.
Significance — fecundity: whether PGSs for immunoassay-measured lab traits partly score binder affinity; whether ancestry differences in reference intervals are partly assay artifacts tracking allele frequency; whether cis-MR of such biomarkers needs a bias-sensitivity analysis of this form; whether calibrators and commutability standards should be proteoform-aware; whether genotype-aware result reporting is net-beneficial; and symmetrically, whether cis effects surviving an orthogonal method identify real proteoform physiology.
Significance — anchoring: the epitope-effect dispute in pQTL studies; HbA1c/G6PD and Hb-variant guidance; FDH, macro-TSH, variant hCG, GDF-15 H202D, F8 assay discrepancy, D-variant typing; Lp(a) isoform-dependent bias and its standardisation fight; the exclusion-restriction problem for cis-MR; IVDR post-market obligations; the equity argument on ancestry-specific reference intervals.
Reason for silence: Primarily expected-signal camouflage in the one community holding both genomes and results — a cis hit in the gene encoding the measured analyte is lab-GWAS's success criterion and positive control, so the single signal that would reveal assay bias is the one nobody interrogates (LabWAS reads its cis hits as biology with no artifact arm). Supported secondarily by split custody (epitopes with manufacturers, genomes with biobanks), an interference ontology in clinical chemistry proper where the patient's genome is not an interferent, and an incentive gap: nobody owns the whole test menu. Weakened at Gate 4: in immunohaematology the patient's genome *is* the recognised and audited cause of discrepant results, and several clinical specialties ask the per-analyte version routinely, so the ontology mechanism holds for clinical chemistry but not for laboratory medicine as a whole; the remainder of the silence is partly explained by data unavailability, i.e. difficulty, which is not an admissible mechanism.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status) — two independent fresh-context adversaries, 9 new-vocabulary Disguise queries each; verbatim logs in batches/2026-10-15-2033/UQ-20261015-19-adversary-1.md and -adversary-2.md. Status below is the worse of the two:
| 1 Triviality | Mechanism settled; six worked cells plus the ≤12% research-platform ceiling make the answer a page of bookkeeping. | Not derivable: no source holds the denominator (carriers among people actually tested per analyte); the ceiling is an LD/structure upper bound on research panels with no patient, threshold or orthogonal arm; six anecdotes are consistent with 0.1 and with 500 crossings per 100,000 tests, and the one computed analyte (G6PD/HbA1c ≈2%) gave a number nobody would have guessed. | Resolved (both) |
| 2 Disguise | Translated out of genomics the class is asked and audited: F8 "assay discrepancy" with dual-assay guidance (2014), FDH/ALB R218H across current clinical FT4 methods with an MS route, D-variant serologic typing with published discordance rates and genotyping policy, IgG allotype confounding of measured antibody levels, Titan 2026 on genetic bias in filtration markers. Gate 2 searched none of these vocabularies, and the record's claim that no field has a slot for genotype is contradicted. | 18 new queries across immunohaematology, thyroid eponyms, nephrology, serology, German, French and answer-seeking phrasings produced no cross-assay census, no per-100,000 crossing rate for routine IVDs, no variant-by-platform interaction in linked care data, no population-scale variant-agnostic orthogonal arm. The estimand has no owner; the serology analogue is qualitative antigen typing and does not transport. But this is a scope extension of asked questions, and the nearest-prior set is materially nearer than Gate 2 recorded. | Partial (both) |
| 3 Combinatorial novelty | Genetics × clinical chemistry with nothing hard at the seam — run a cis scan and read off platform terms. | The seam is the problem: assay bias and proteoform physiology make the same prediction for limb (a), so a discriminator must be manufactured, and both candidate discriminators have variant-sensitivity failure modes (P5). Hemophilia A shows a case where the two methods disagree because the protein really behaves differently; FDH and GDF-15 show the interface biting the other way. | Resolved (both) |
| 4 Presupposition failure | P2 is load-bearing and asserted: no cohort is named in which the same people have the same analyte by routine immunoassay and by a variant-agnostic orthogonal method at estimable N. P1 is weaker than conceded (UKB biochemistry centrally run on fixed platforms; primary-care extracts analyzer-blind; LOINC rarely identifies reagent), so limb (b) is likely not estimable. The pre-specified fallback covers only (b), not (c); without (c), (a)+(d) count crossings among carriers, which real biology produces as readily as binder failure, so the headline misclassification rate is unidentified. | All presuppositions are declared contested and the census is a deliverable; (a) and (d) remain estimable with no platform metadata; LOINC's Method axis and endocrine pathways that order both dialysis FT4 and MS testosterone make (c) non-empty in principle, and the census could be extended to (c). But neither adversary could evidence a qualifying paired subset from a query, and the record does not take that route. | Partial (both) |
| 5 Vagueness | Three pre-specified outcomes mean the project cannot fail to report something; the equivalence band's width is unstated and decides the answer; the feasibility census is a metadata audit relabelled as an answer about patients. | Each limb is falsifiable on its own terms (replication, interaction test, equivalence band in both directions, crossings with CIs); a bounded null is a legitimate answer to a prevalence question; the census is labelled a lesser pre-declared deliverable, not the question answered. Band width is a pre-registration detail. | Partial (adversary 2; Resolved for adversary 1) |
| 6 Significance inflation | Every precedent (dual-FVIII assays, FDH reflex practice, HbA1c Hb-variant guidance, RHD genotyping) was adopted on case series and method comparisons, never on a prevalence estimate, so a per-100,000 rate is not the missing input; manufacturer action additionally needs epitope disclosure that is proprietary, and no evidence shows CLSI or IFCC wants a genotype arm. | The same precedent list proves the audiences are movable; laboratory directors and guideline writers can act with no disclosure; the lab-GWAS/cis-MR licence consequence is real and unprobed, now independently evidenced by Titan 2026. But "a number is what unblocks insert warnings and standards committees" is asserted, not shown. | Partial (adversary 1; Resolved for adversary 2) |
| 7 Reason for silence | Camouflage explains neglect in genomics, not silence in the clinical specialties that ask the per-analyte version routinely; the ontology mechanism is damaged by immunohaematology, where the patient's genome is the audited cause of discordance; split custody and new instrument are reasons it is hard to answer, which Gate 4 does not accept. | Camouflage survives as a genuine asking-level mechanism for the one community holding genomes and results, with LabWAS as concrete support; ontology mismatch holds for clinical chemistry proper; the incentive gap is admissible. Camouflage demoted from sole to primary-among-partial, and per Gate 4's own rule this sent novelty back for another look — which attack 2 supplied, and which understated the prior set. | Partial (both) |
| 8 Dissolution | "Is the assay wrong or is the protein different?" may have no fact of the matter: once a reference method is fixed, bias is definitional, and limb (c) measures method-dependence and relabels it bias. Hemophilia A is the worked case where both numbers are true about different things. | Outcome (d) is dissolution-proof — whether a reported number crossed a decision line and whether carriers' care diverged are facts under any convention — and (b)'s variant-by-platform interaction is a fact about instruments. Thresholds are defined on stated reference methods, so carrier-specific deviation from that method is bias non-circularly. But (c)'s interpretive core narrows to a commutability/standardisation question an existing community owns, and (d) lacks an outcome anchor showing the care was wrong. | Partial (both) |
Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 3/3
Strongest remaining objection: limb (c) — the only limb that separates binder failure from proteoform physiology — rests on a data substrate nobody has shown exists (no named biobank with the same people measured for the same analyte by a routine immunoassay and by a variant-agnostic orthogonal method at estimable N), and the pre-specified fallback declares only limb (b) not estimable; if (c) is unavailable, (a)+(d) count threshold crossings among carriers, which genuine biology produces as readily as assay bias, so the headline "misclassification per 100,000 tests" is not identified. Every cell of this table filled so far was filled by recruiting and measuring people, not by mining linked records.
Promotion requires: naming a concrete cohort or linkage that satisfies P2 (paired routine immunoassay and variant-agnostic orthogonal results for the same analyte in the same people, at an N supporting CIs) and extending the pre-specified fallback to a failure of limb (c) so the headline estimand stays identified; plus a Gate 2 redo that opens PMC7222281 and PMC7408830 and states how the candidate differs from FDH/ALB R218H across current FT4 methods, and re-sources the candidate as a cross-field transplant rather than a new-instrument question, with novelty re-rated on that record.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): run and publish the feasibility census before any association testing — inventory LOINC Method-axis and analyzer/reagent metadata coverage in UK Biobank primary-care and hospital extracts and All of Us, and enumerate analytes with both immunoassay and non-affinity results in overlapping participants. That census decides whether limbs (b) and (c) exist at all, and is the pre-registered deliverable either way.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): None — not rejected; no row added to routed-open-problems.md.
