ID: UQ-20261016-35
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine/biology — biobank and cohort research methods; secondary: statistics (finite-sample robustness, non-ignorable attrition), survey methodology, data-protection scholarship, machine unlearning. Source method: silence mapping.
Question (canonical): In a biobank operating a deletion-on-withdrawal mandate, using dated withdrawal-ID tranches and a pre-fixed panel of headline estimates (k GWAS associations, k' hazard ratios, one polygenic score's discrimination): (a) what is the pre-deletion standardised difference between withdrawn and retained participants on the exposures, covariates and outcomes the cohort is actually used to study; (b) how far does each headline estimate move when recomputed on the frame immediately before and immediately after each tranche, against its Monte Carlo error and pre-declared decision boundaries; and (c) does the cumulative movement accumulate monotonically in the direction (a) predicts — systematic drift rather than noise?
Alternative formulations: What does the right to withdraw do to the scientific record a biobank has already produced? · Are consent-revokers systematically different, on the very variables the cohort studies, from those who stay, and how much do published estimates change when they are removed? · (method-field) How does the realised influence of the actually-withdrawn subset compare with the worst-case influence of an adversarially chosen subset of the same size, and is it signed and cumulative?
Motivating gap: Withdrawal's "how" is densely operational, its "so what" absent. UK Biobank's "Participant withdrawals on UKB-RAP" (opened) mandates that withdrawn data be "no longer accessed, analysed, or retained", asserts removal "supports the accuracy and validity of research outputs", and is silent on existing results, re-analysis, and any withdrawal count. Adjacent literatures are about entry (participation bias) and outcome ascertainment (dropout), not retrospective deletion of already-analysed data.
Presuppositions: P1 withdrawals numerous enough to move anything — ESTABLISHED at one custodian (HUNT2 1,187/65,291 = 1.9%, Ursin 2020, opened), but see A1: that is a sample-withdrawal rate, not a deletion rate, and UKB's lost_to_flup.pdf documents a withdrawal category under which prior data stay usable. P2 earlier/later frames both exist — CONTESTED; the mandate works against it. P3 custodian may lawfully retain a pre-deletion aggregate — CONTESTED (the legal-block outcome is declared an answer). P4 withdrawal is not the informative censoring attrition methods handle — ESTABLISHED structurally, CONTESTED in magnitude. P5 someone acts — CONTESTED. P6 deletion actually executed by every copy-holder — CONTESTED, and sharpened at the late Gate 4: the claim that public repositories hold dated withdrawal-ID lists is refuted (authenticated per-Application download, per-Application ID recoding, repositories exposing only private paths and filtering code), but one opened primary does establish that researchers can hold both frames at once — the ALSPAC/ARIES team held a 2015 and a 2018 frame of the same cohort and could see which participants were in one and not the other. So the irreversibility is de jure rather than de facto, which is itself the finding. P7 withdrawal motives not required — FLAGGED, load-bearing for novelty.
What would count as an answer: (a) a custodian-side analysis run once under governance before destruction, reporting withdrawer-vs-retained distributions on a pre-specified variable set plus the change in a pre-specified estimate panel across each tranche; or (b) a researcher-side equivalent from dated releases and archived derived files with withdrawal-ID lists as the only linkage; benchmarked against the worst-case (AMIP) shift for the same subset size. All within Monte Carlo error → non-issue, practice licensed. Any estimate across a decision boundary → an unquantified, growing, custodian-only-measurable erosion term. Legally unrunnable → the erosion term is unidentifiable to every party (a governance result with the same audience). Limb (c)'s sign test separates drift from noise.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 Gate 2 searches in five vocabularies + 7 fetches (3 returned content); full list at batches/2026-10-16-1233/UQ-20261016-35-record.md. Most informative: `characteristics of participants who withdraw consent from a biobank cohort study` → motives/ethics only, no withdrawer-vs-retained comparison, no recomputation; `dropping a little data change conclusions finite-sample robustness metric` → Broderick/Giordano/Meager AMIP (the method-owning field, found in strength); `UK Biobank number of participants withdrawn consent` → custodian operational pages, no count or rate; `machine unlearning deletion requests not random distribution shift bias remaining dataset` → model-fidelity/privacy framing only (NB: contradicted at Gate 4); answer-directed `UK Biobank results differ between data releases ... withdrawn participants removed` → replication-of-other-studies paper plus a forum post, no consequence analysis. Gate 4 added 18 further searches in new vocabularies (9 per adversary, minimum 8 met each) and 8 fetches; see UQ-20261016-35-adversary-1.md and -2.md.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): **N1** Broderick, Giordano & Meager, "An Automatic Finite-Sample Robustness Metric: When Can Dropping a Little Data Make a Big Difference?", arXiv:2011.14999 (opened) — unit: observations; endpoint: sign change/loss of significance in a quantity of interest; comparator: full-sample estimate; estimand: Maximum Influence Perturbation, worst case over admissible subsets. **N4 (Gate 4, decisive)** Elmas, "The Impact of Data Persistence Bias on Social Media Studies", WebSci '23, arXiv:2303.00902 (opened by adversary #2) — unit: removed accounts/posts; endpoint: the construct the corpora measure (mean political-orientation score 0.15 → −0.23) *and* a re-run published framing analysis on the degraded frame; comparator: a retained pre-deletion archive (Internet Archive Twitter Stream Grab, in which deleted tweets are not removed); estimand: the realised shift from a non-random governance/platform-driven deletion stream. **N5 (Gate 4)** Tazare et al., "NHS national data opt-outs: trends and potential consequences for health data research", BJGP Open 2024 (opened by adversary #2) — unit: patients opting out; endpoint: opt-out prevalence by age, sex, region (2.77% → 4.97%); comparator: national population; estimand: governance-driven removal rate and its demographic gradient, with the explicit statement that characteristics of opt-outs are "not available" and that "once an individual has opted out, their data is no longer available to researchers who wish to study these mechanisms". Also opened at Gate 4: PMC6287151 Table 1, "Characteristics of participants who declined the consent versus those who continued in the cohort" (n=54 vs 809; age, sex, education, stroke/disability; all p 0.182–0.892) — limb (a), published, in a biomedical cohort; and Hillman et al., JAMA Oncol 2023;9(8):1041–1047 (9% withdrawal over 2 years; Hispanic ethnicity OR 1.67, placebo design OR 1.64, age ≥75 OR 1.39), limb (a) asked and answered in the trial regime with bias and power consequences named. Ursin et al. 2020 (10.1007/s11019-020-09969-w, opened) confirmed real by both adversaries; it is a source for P1, not a competitor. UKB "Participant withdrawals on UKB-RAP" confirmed real.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs N1 — realised rather than worst-case shift, unit defined by a governance act, plus limb (a) and a repeated-tranche direction test N1's single-perturbation framing lacks. vs N4 — different data class (human participants under GDPR withdrawal vs posts under platform ToS), different estimates (frame ranks vs hazard ratios and PGS discrimination), and no surviving archive of the earlier frame. vs N5 — N5 quantifies the removal rate and its gradient but cannot run limb (a) or (b) and says so. These differences are real, and they are not enough: N4 poses the same question under its own name ("data persistence bias") and executes limbs (a) and (b), N5 poses the health-data version in its title, and PMC6287151/Hillman publish limb (a) for consent-decliners and trial withdrawers. What remains unprecedented is an unrun measurement in a new data class — a corpus swap on an asked question — not an unposed question. The record's load-bearing negative ("none treats the deleted subset's covariate profile as a quantity to be measured before it disappears") is false as stated and is struck.
Novelty confidence: Medium (Gate 2 graded Medium; adversary 2 reduced it to Low on a prior whose working leg verification then refuted; adversary 3, run cold with five sources opened, re-graded Medium, which the judge adopts)
Grounds: no opened source runs limb (a) on a real retroactive-deletion stream, or limb (c)'s direction test, and the two nearest neighbours each explicitly remove or declare unavailable the quantity the candidate wants. Not High, and the reason is the close neighbour that makes this Provisional: Tazare et al. 2024 publishes, for a sibling consent mechanism in the largest health-data system in the UK, the rate, the reasoning that bias follows if revocation propensity relates to exposure or outcome, a simulated magnitude, and the candidate's own irreversibility verdict verbatim — the governance half of the payload is already in print for a neighbouring mechanism. PMC6287151 adds a four-variable miniature of limb (a) in a regime where the data were kept.
Significance — consequence: If (b)/(c) positive, biobank results carry an erosion term that is unquantified, monotonically growing and post hoc unmeasurable, with a named remedy (mandatory retained pre-deletion aggregate; versioned citable frame identifiers). If null at realistic rates, current practice is licensed with a number and N1's alarm is calibrated for this data class. Honest prior: at 0.1–2% removal from n≈500,000, headline estimates are very unlikely to move materially, so consequence concentrates in subgroup/rare-variant estimates, near-threshold estimates, and the identifiability finding.
Significance — audience: Biobank custodians (hold both frames and the procedure); RECs/IRBs and DPOs who drafted the erasure derogation; journals/funders/reproducibility bodies (frame versioning is their lever); machine unlearning (realised-case test of its harmless-removal premise — though arXiv 2302.03350 and 2311.10385 show that literature does model non-uniform deletion, so this limb is weaker than the record claimed). Discount: the audience best placed to answer is the one a positive answer embarrasses. Direct negative evidence added at the late Gate 4, which the record did not have: Tazare et al. 2024 made this argument to this audience in a peer-reviewed journal, and opt-outs stood at 5.40% as of January 2024 with no policy response in the paper's own account. Two counterweights, both from opened sources: the candidate's ask is far smaller than Tazare's implied national policy change — one retained aggregate table and a versioned frame identifier, added to a workflow the custodian already executes — and nobody has proposed it, so it is not a remedy already declined; and the FDA/OHRP trial regime shows a regulator acting on identical reasoning, mandating that already-collected data "may not be removed" because the study "must remain ... scientifically valid" and the bias potential is "immense".
Significance — fecundity: Minimal lawful pre-deletion aggregate for permanent frame auditability; withdrawal-propensity modelling and its own ethics; whether a deletion-sensitivity statistic belongs in cohort reporting standards; joint satisfiability of deletion and reproducibility mandates; transport across consent regimes; calibration of unlearning's harmless-removal assumption.
Significance — anchoring: GDPR Art. 17 and research derogations; reproducibility/data-availability debate; influence-function and case-deletion robustness; participation bias in UK Biobank; informative censoring, MNAR and refreshment-sample identification (which deletion defeats); right-to-be-forgotten; HUNT's 2002 withdrawal episode as the only documented large dated tranche.
Reason for silence: Claimed: (1) an incentive-and-authority gap — only the custodian can compute it, at the moment of a legal deletion, against its own interest; (2) a disciplinary/framing boundary routing withdrawal to ethics while the method-owning field never meets the word. Both were graded failed on Gate 4 evidence by the first two adversaries; both gradings are now corrected. Against (1) they cited 35 public UK Biobank analysis repositories applying dated withdrawal-ID CSVs to frames they already hold. Verification refuted the public-availability half of that: the repositories expose private filesystem paths and the filtering code, never the list; the download is authenticated and per-Application; and participant IDs are re-coded per Application, so a withdrawal list is not a portable key into the cohort. Against (2) they cited the fields meeting in web science and health-data research. Adversary 3, run cold, found a better and sharper version of the same point in a single opened primary — the ALSPAC/ARIES EWAS-across-versions paper names "withdraw consent to share their data" in its Introduction and "withdrawal of consent for certain individuals" in its Discussion, and then removes the mechanism by restricting to the 946 overlapping participants and attributing the remainder to preprocessing. So the record's specific claim that the two literatures' vocabularies never meet is REFUTED, and what replaces it is stronger than either the record's mechanism or the adversaries' dismissal: a team that held both frames, named the mechanism twice, and designed it away is not a team that failed to think of the question but a team with no method for a specific, exogenously selected, governance-generated deleted subset — its only available tool bounding the worst case over hypothetical subsets, a family that has never been applied to cohort data. That is a method-availability gap at a disciplinary boundary, which the ledger admits, and it is now evidenced in a primary source rather than inferred from a query log. The authority limb survives independently and is also evidenced: Tazare et al. 2024 is a competent team wanting the covariate contrast and reporting it "not available". The "nobody thought it worth asking" story is therefore contested rather than settled, and the FDA/OHRP regulator facing the same magnitude judgement in trials called the bias potential "immense".

Verification by the run session (the Gate 4 Disguise kill was fatal and rested on one paper said to be doing the candidate's work under another name, so that paper and the counter-claim carried with it were checked; independent fresh-context checker, 8 web searches and 6 GitHub code-search probes with 6 fetches, no refusals; full log in batches/2026-10-16-1233/UQ-20261016-35-verification.md). Both legs fail.
(i) The claim that Elmas 2023 already executes the candidate's limbs FAILS on its working leg. Elmas, "The Impact of Data Persistence Bias on Social Media Studies" (arXiv:2303.00902, WebSci '23), keeps the original dataset throughout — that retention IS the method: turnout is "the number of tweets we could collect" divided "by the number of tweets in the original dataset". Nothing is mandated and nothing is irreversible. The removal is removal from the platform, not from the researcher; the stated causes are "account suspension is the biggest factor in tweet removals as 54% of the tweets are uncollectable due to it across all datasets", "The second biggest factor is deletions, which account for 34% of the removals" and protected accounts at 10%; and of the last the paper says "accounts may switch back and forth between protected status to public status". The words "irreversible" and "rehydration" do not appear, and no duty on researchers to delete already-collected data appears anywhere in it — reading Twitter's developer terms into the paper is the reviewer's inference, not the paper's content. The biobank case is the structural inverse: the deletion mandate destroys exactly the retained pre-deletion frame that makes Elmas's measurement possible. Its unit is tweets, authors and whole topic-datasets rather than persons with covariates, and its endpoint is turnout plus aggregate composition shifts with no exposure-outcome association anywhere in it, so the candidate's limb (a) has no counterpart in it at all. Limb (b) has an aggregate, non-person-level counterpart and only that: Elmas does show removal is non-random with respect to an attribute measured before removal, by correlating turnout with the mean political-orientation score of trends — "The Pearson correlation is -0.38 and is statistically significant (p < 0001)", as printed.
(ii) The counter-claim carried in the same kill — that dated withdrawal-ID files are already in third-party hands, so the drift is measurable from outside — is REFUTED. The file naming is right (w11867_20210201.csv, w11867_20200204.csv, w11867_20210809.csv, w11867_20220222.csv, withdraw81499_55_20230915.txt and ukb_withdrawn_individuals_8Feb2021.id all appear in public analysis code, so dated local snapshots do exist and are retained by analysis groups), but the distribution channel is authenticated and per-Application: UK Biobank's own instructions have the PI or an approved delegate sign in to the access management system, open the Application in Showcase and "download the latest withdrawal list and apply it to your dataset", and the public repositories expose only private filesystem paths and the filtering code, never the file. Six GitHub code-search probes for the lists themselves returned nothing — a strong negative rather than a proof, since code search does not index every blob. And a defeater the kill did not consider: UK Biobank participant IDs are re-coded per Application, which is why bridging link files exist in the same corpus, so a withdrawal list is meaningful only against the frame of its own Application and is not a portable public key into the cohort.
(iii) The kill's secondary priors were not opened and remain unverified: Tazare 2024, PMC6287151 Table 1 (consent-decliners) and Hillman, JAMA Oncol 2023 (trial withdrawers) — all three on populations structurally unlike a biobank withdrawer whose data must be deleted. What the checker's own sweep found instead is that the biobank-withdrawal literature is motives, attitudes and trust, qualitative or survey-based, with no covariate comparison of withdrawers against retained participants; and that UK Biobank's own lost-to-follow-up documentation cuts against the record, since its code 5 is "Participant has withdrawn consent for future linkage", of whom "UK Biobank still has permission to use their clinical information and samples collected previously" — not the deletion case the candidate asks about. The literature that does pose a deletion-induced-drift question is machine unlearning (arXiv:2302.03350, arXiv:2411.17126), which is about models rather than cohort estimates and supplies no pre-deletion-frame comparison.
(iv) The candidate's drift question is NOT FOUND posed in print for a consent-withdrawal biobank on 8 web queries and 6 code-search probes. One source was partly unreadable and is recorded as such: the withdrawal subsection of UK Biobank's GDPR notice.

It opened five sources, two of which the record had only named, and it resolved the record's load-bearing unverified residue. | # | Attack | Objection | Best response | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Triviality | Largely answerable in a page for the limb that carries the headline. Removing a fraction p inflates a standard error by 1/sqrt(1-p), which at p = 0.019 is a factor of 1.0096 — about a 1% widening of the interval — and at n about 500,000 that is nothing, as the record's own significance section concedes. The one opened source that quantifies anything here does the page already: Tazare et al. 2024's simulation gives power 80% to 78% at 5% removal and to 71% at 20%, with an illustrative null odds ratio of 0.9996 (95% CI 0.98 to 1.02). And limb (a)'s sign is guessable from the attrition literature's standing result that leavers are less educated, poorer and sicker. | The page answers the variance question and the random-removal question; the candidate's is the bias question under non-random removal, and Tazare is explicit that its own simulation does not cover it, for the stated reason that "further information on clinical and sociodemographic characteristics of patients opting out is not available". The 1/sqrt(1-p) scaling bounds dispersion, not displacement: a p-fraction removal with a standardised difference on the exposure or outcome displaces an estimate by an amount governed by that difference and p and NOT damped by sqrt(n), so the large-n reassurance is a non-sequitur for the bias term. The regime where it bites is the one the record isolates — small effective n: for a variant at MAF 0.001 in n = 500,000 under Hardy-Weinberg, expected heterozygotes are about 999, and a 1.9% removal takes about 19 of them (binomial SD about 4.3), with whether those 19 are a random 19 being exactly what the deletion makes unanswerable (the adversary's own arithmetic, assumptions stated). And limb (a) is not answerable from the attrition page, because the literature with a mature position on withdrawal is the trial literature, which never faced deletion: FDA/OHRP guidance says already-collected data "may not be removed". | Partial |
| 2 | Disguise | Two renamings come very close, both outside the record's five vocabularies. Gate 4 completeness and how the verdict was reached: three independent adversaries, all with their Disguise sweeps executed, so Disguise is verified. Adversary 2 returned attack 2 Unresolved, which is fatal, and both earlier adversaries returned attack 7 Unresolved; the batch rejected on the former. Verification then checked the attack-2 kill against its sources and found both legs failing — Elmas 2023 retains the original dataset and measures loss of re-collectability, with nothing mandated and nothing irreversible, and the counter-claim that dated withdrawal-ID files are already in third-party hands is refuted by the authenticated per-Application distribution channel and the per-Application recoding of participant IDs. The same check removed the evidential core of the attack-7 Unresolved, which rested on the claim that public repositories hold the lists. Adversary 3 then ran cold at the strict standard and returned three Resolved and five Partial with nothing Unresolved, grading attack 7 Partial on a better-evidenced mechanism than either earlier adversary had. So no objection stands Unresolved on the best available evidence, and the entry moves from Rejected to Provisional — on the Medium-novelty-with-a-close-neighbour clause rather than on a surviving objection. What would restore Rejected: a sourced Unresolved on attacks 1, 2 or 4, most plausibly by showing that some published work has run limb (a) on a real retroactive-deletion stream, or that Tazare's declared-unidentifiable result already settles the identifiability finding for the biobank mechanism too.
Record corrections compelled by adversary 3, from sources it opened:
- The record's P6-adjacent claim that "35 public UK Biobank analysis repositories apply dated withdrawal-ID CSVs ... so thousands of approved projects have held both frames and the ID list simultaneously" is NOT supported as written, and the verification pass refuted the public-availability half of it: the repositories expose private filesystem paths and the filtering code, never the list, the download is authenticated and per-Application, and participant IDs are re-coded per Application so a list is not a portable key into the cohort. What IS evidenced, and is stronger for being a single opened primary, is that the ALSPAC/ARIES team held a 2015 frame and a 2018 frame of a real cohort at once and could see which participants were in one and not the other.
- The record's load-bearing unverified residue PMC6287151 is RESOLVED. It is a four-variable table (DOI 10.1155/2018/8267948, published 26 November 2018) captioned "Characteristics of participants who declined the consent versus those who continued in the cohort", comparing 54 who declined against 809 who continued on mean age, proportion of women, primary-school education, and stroke or severe disability, with no p-value below 0.05. It recomputes no estimate, and its existence proves the decliners' baseline data were RETAINED rather than deleted. The adversary records, rather than resolves, that "declined the consent" is ambiguous between refusing to continue and refusing entry, and that the article title was not exposed on the table page. This is simultaneously the candidate's best argument and its sharpest limitation: the comparison is routine where data persist and unavailable where they do not.
Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness: held at 3/3 on the Gate 1 reformulation, which fixes the unit, the pre-named estimate panel, the comparator frames, the Monte Carlo-error scale and the sign test, and pre-declares all three outcomes including the legally-blocked one. Adversary 3 graded vagueness Resolved for that version and Partial for the canonical version alone, and its one falsification lands on the canonical wording rather than on the operative formulation. One amendment is nevertheless compelled and is recorded under Promotion: the canonical version's "nobody can measure" is false as a factual claim and must read "unmeasurable by any party acting within the withdrawal terms".
Significance: 2/3, now with evidence on both sides rather than on one. Against: the closest published instance of this argument — Tazare et al. 2024, same reasoning, same audience, peer-reviewed — produced no visible policy movement, and opt-outs stood at 5.40% as of January 2024. For: the candidate's ask is far smaller than Tazare's (one retained aggregate table and a versioned frame identifier, inside a workflow the custodian already executes at the moment of deletion, and nobody has proposed it); a regulator has already acted on identical reasoning in the adjacent trial regime, where already-collected data "may not be removed"; and the data-version reproducibility community is an uptake-ready audience that had this channel in its hands and designed it away.
Strongest remaining objection: a narrowing rather than a kill, assembled from attacks 1, 2 and 6 together. Tazare et al. 2024 has already published, for a sibling consent mechanism in the largest health-data system in the UK, the rate (5.40% as of January 2024), the reasoning that bias follows if the exclusion propensity relates to exposure or outcome, a simulated magnitude (power 80% to 78% at 5% removal), and — verbatim — the candidate's own irreversibility verdict: the characteristics of those who opted out are "not available" and the bias cannot be reliably corrected. The governance half of this candidate's payload is therefore already in print for a neighbouring mechanism, and it moved nothing. What remains genuinely unperformed is the realised measurement itself on a true retroactive-deletion stream — limb (a) on the cohort's own exposure and outcome set, and limb (c)'s direction test — and the record overstates how much of the rest is new. The earlier objection, that the whole question is a corpus swap on Elmas 2023, is withdrawn: Elmas retains the original dataset throughout and measures loss of re-collectability, with nothing mandated and nothing irreversible, which is the structural inverse of this case.
Promotion requires: (i) retiring the canonical wording in favour of the Gate 1 reformulation, with the irreversibility clause rewritten as "unmeasurable by any party acting within the withdrawal terms" — the present "nobody can measure" is false as a factual claim, since the ALSPAC/ARIES team demonstrably held both frames; (ii) restating the novelty claim as the realised measurement on a true retroactive-deletion stream, explicitly conceding that the worry, the rate, a simulated magnitude and the irreversibility verdict are already in print for the opt-out mechanism; (iii) establishing a deletion rate rather than a sample-withdrawal rate, since P1 still rests on a figure the cold adversary did not open and which the record itself calls possibly atypical, and no custodian in its search results publishes a withdrawal count; (iv) pre-registering the estimate panel before any frame is touched, which is the operative safeguard against boundary-shopping and the thing that keeps attack 5 Resolved. With (i) to (iii) done and the close-neighbour concession made explicit, the entry's remaining content is a measurement nobody has performed, and it could be Validated.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): read Tazare et al. 2024 first and in full, because it is the close neighbour that bounds the claim and it supplies the one thing the candidate needs most — a worked statement of why limb (a) is unidentifiable from the researcher side, which is the premise the custodian-side design exists to overturn. Then approach a custodian with the smallest version of the ask: at the moment a tranche is deleted, retain one aggregate table of the pre-named variable set and a versioned frame identifier. Nothing else in the question is reachable without that step, and the enforced-withdrawal date of 1 April 2026 means the tranches are being generated now.
Routing: not routed. The entry is Provisional, so it is not an already-asked rejection, and the candidate's drift question was independently confirmed NOT FOUND posed in print for a consent-withdrawal biobank by both the verification checker and adversary 3. Recorded for completeness, and deliberately NOT routed: Tazare et al. 2024 states that the characteristics of opted-out individuals are "not available" and that the bias cannot be reliably corrected. That is a declaration of impossibility rather than a question posed and left open, so it fails the routing test — a row on it would hand the research workstream a problem its own source says cannot be answered from the researcher side.

ID: UQ-20261016-36
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine/biology — cryobiology, ART laboratories, biobanking, cell-therapy manufacturing. Adjacent vocabularies checked: veterinary reproduction, cryogenic thermometry/metrology, cold-chain/mean-kinetic-temperature methodology, statistical batch-effect modelling, pharma GxP chamber qualification.
Question (canonical): Within a single ART or cell-therapy facility, among cryostored units of one specimen class frozen under one protocol, what share of the residual between-unit variance in a per-unit post-thaw endpoint is attributable to the unit's static storage coordinate (vessel, canister, rack, height), estimated with cohort, calendar date, donor and operator adjusted and with re-racking and tank-transfer events as the identifying variation, and what is the effect size per 10 °C of a pre-specified time-weighted static storage temperature derived from the facility's own thermal map? (Gate 1 reformulation; it is the version judged here.)
Alternative formulations:
- Gate 0 intake version (compound, recorded and superseded): does a unit's recorded storage coordinate plus the retrieval-event history of its neighbourhood predict post-thaw outcome, and does between-facility variation in in-dewar thermal history account for part of the published between-facility spread in post-thaw survival? The retrieval-exposure limb is answered (Prior 1) and the between-facility limb had no identified estimand; both were dropped by the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation.
- Is a frozen sample's shelf position in the tank an unrecognised exposure variable for its post-thaw viability?
Motivating gap: Vertical temperature non-uniformity inside vapour-phase LN2 dewars is measured and modelled (order 8–14 °C) and transient warming of neighbouring inventory during retrieval is documented, but no study attaches either to per-unit post-thaw outcomes via the inventory coordinate, and no published variance decomposition of post-thaw outcome contains a storage-location term. Gate 2 correction: the intake's claim that upper positions sit near the ~−130 °C glass transition is not supported — the warmest measured position was −181.5 °C (CBS V-1500, nine probes, 24 h) and the warmest modelled monitoring-point average −165.4 °C (Xiong et al. 2026), against Tg −126 to −121 °C. The gradient is real but ~10 °C, not ~60 °C.
Presuppositions:
1. Per-unit storage coordinate recorded and retrievable — ESTABLISHED (Prior 1 logged cane, canister and tank position for all 9,200 cycles); contested for legacy archives.
2. The gradient reaches the devitrification/glass-transition region — CONTESTED, not falsified. Both position-resolved sources put every occupied position 35–65 °C below Tg, but the measured one is a near-empty isothermal vessel marketed for uniformity, and the record's reading of Prior 2 (risk confined to a lifting *neck* transient) is unsupported by the source it cites, which describes −50/−70 °C as vapour-phase temperatures within the dewar and warns that vapour-phase *storage* carries devitrification risk. The reformulated question needs only a non-zero gradient, which is established.
3. Retrieval/opening events reconstructable — ESTABLISHED at one facility, with explicit bystander-counting rules (Prior 1).
4. A per-unit post-thaw endpoint exists and is linkable — ESTABLISHED for ART and cell therapy; false for many research biobanks.
5. Position not fully confounded with calendar time, cohort or donor — CONTESTED; the main design threat, confirmed in Prior 1's data (storage time ≈83 → ≈301 days across exposure groups, P < 0.001). This is why the re-racking/tank-transfer instrument is load-bearing.
6. Sub-Tg degradation cumulative and monotone in temperature and time — CONTESTED; no quantitative sub-Tg rate law for the −195/−180 regime was sourced by either the record or the adversary.
7. Separable from protocol variance at achievable sample sizes — CONTESTED; a 9,200-cycle study could not resolve the larger retrieval exposure.
What would count as an answer: A within-facility analysis of a few thousand units of one specimen class with (a) storage coordinate, (b) a thermal history logged at several heights or reconstructed from a mapped gradient, and (c) a per-unit post-thaw endpoint; outcome regressed on coordinate and on a pre-specified time-weighted thermal summary, cohort/date/donor/operator adjusted, identified off re-racking and tank transfers. Deliverable: a variance component for storage location plus an effect size per 10 °C, judged against a pre-registered null band from the facility's own replicate variability. A null in a facility with a documented gradient counts as an answer.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 20 distinct queries (11 Gate 2 + 9 adversary) and 9 fetches (1 dead: PMC6123768 returned a reCAPTCHA interstitial). Full lists: batches/2026-10-16-1433/UQ-20261016-36-record.md and UQ-20261016-36-adversary-1.md. Most informative: (a) mandatory own-field title query `effect of storage position in liquid nitrogen tank on post-thaw survival of cryopreserved embryos` → Prior 1 plus storage-*duration* papers only; (b) `variance components post-thaw viability attributable to storage versus freezing protocol operator donor` → no published variance decomposition containing a storage-location term; (c) adversary's statistics-vocabulary replication `"variance component" OR "random effect" freezer "shelf position" OR "storage location" biospecimen ... confounded storage time` → storage-time papers only, independently reproducing that negative; (d) method-owning-field query on cumulative thermal-dose/MKT and excursion budgeting → the method family is mature and migrating into cryogenics but has never been applied to in-dewar position; (e) adversary's pharma-GxP query → the regulated response to intra-chamber non-uniformity is to qualify the warmest location and place worst case there, i.e. a control rather than a study; (f) answer-side query `"position in the tank" ... did not affect post-thaw survival` → no published null or positive on static in-tank position versus outcome.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
1. Zhang H, Ye D, Wu Y, Li Y, Huang X (2023), "Effect of exposed-to-air frequency of cryopreserved embryo on clinical outcomes of vitrified-warmed embryo transfer cycles: a retrospective analysis of 9,200 vitrified-warmed transfer cycles", BMC Pregnancy Childbirth, DOI 10.1186/s12884-023-05879-w — unit: the transfer cycle (n = 9,200); endpoint: clinical pregnancy and live birth, with post-warming survival among the outcomes; comparator: EAF = 2; estimand: adjusted OR for a cumulative retrieval-*event count* (the paper states the count is used "rather than duration time of exposed-to-air"); result null (D3 EAF ≥10, clinical pregnancy OR 0.867, 95% CI 0.672–1.119). Built its exposure from logged cane/canister/tank coordinates, counted bystander events, and did not analyse the static coordinate. Verified in full text by the adversary.
2. Sansinena MJ, Santos MV, Taminelli GL, Zaritzky NE (2014), "Implications of storage and handling conditions on glass transition and potential devitrification of oocytes and embryos", Theriogenology 82(3):373–378 — unit: a modelled straw carrier plus DSC on a vitrification solution; endpoint: Tg (−126 to −121 °C) and devitrification onset (−109 °C); comparator: full immersion at −196 °C vs two vapour-phase temperatures (−50/−70 °C); estimand: deterministic time-to-threshold (order 30 s). Citation corrected by the adversary from the UCA repository item the record used; scope per the CONICET record covers exposure "either during storage or upon its removal" (repository record read, not full text).
3. Xiong Z et al. (2026), "Temperature Evolution in Liquid-Nitrogen Biobanks", Applied Sciences 16(15):7700, DOI 10.3390/app16157700 — unit: a CFD monitoring point; endpoint: vapour temperature and between-point spread; comparator: load states; estimand: a simulated physical field. Averages −187.9 → −183.2 °C (automated) and −169.7 → −165.4 °C (non-automated); spreads 10.67 → 13.70 °C and 7.81 → 10.25 °C. No outcome of any kind.
Also: CBS/BioLife "Isothermal Temperature Uniformity Testing" WP-CBS-230500_R01 (2023), nine probes at three heights in a V-1500, warmest hourly reading −181.5 °C — vendor-published, near-empty chamber. And, found by the adversary and absent from the record: Vysekantsev IP et al. (2020), "Effect of Storage Temperature Variations on Viability of Cryopreserved Cells of Pro- and Eukaryotes", Problems of Cryobiology and Cryomedicine — experimentally reports "extradeath" when storage temperature is varied from −196 up to −130 and −100 °C, human embryos among the cells; abstract only, no numbers, no position variable.
Novelty — how this differs from each: From Prior 1 — all four attributes differ: unit (stored unit vs transfer cycle), endpoint (per-unit post-thaw readout vs clinical pregnancy/live birth), comparator (position/thermal contrast vs EAF = 2) and estimand (variance share and per-10 °C effect vs adjusted OR on an event count). Prior 1 answers the retrieval-exposure limb that Gate 1 dropped; it held the static coordinate and did not analyse it. From Prior 2 — a deterministic threshold time, not a per-unit statistical association; it supplies physics the candidate's mechanism needs but does not estimate anything about stored position. From Prior 3 — supplies the exposure field with no outcome attached; the candidate joins such a field to per-unit outcomes. From Vysekantsev et al. — a controlled temperature-dose experiment at and above Tg with no position variable and no observational per-unit estimand; it is the closest neighbour on the per-10 °C limb and it blocks any "obviously zero" dismissal.
Novelty confidence: Medium
[Gate 2 recorded Low; revised here. The Low grade rested on Prior 1 being the candidate's dominant limb, but that limb was removed by the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation, and on the ledger's own test Prior 1 differs from the surviving question on unit, endpoint, comparator and estimand — the named failure mode of grading novelty on a prior aimed at an adjacent object. The surviving estimand was not found published in 20 queries across ten vocabularies, including an independent replication of the key negative in statistics words. Medium, not High, because Prior 1 is close on mechanism and data source and Vysekantsev et al. is close on the temperature-dose limb. Gate 4 had already been run against the Gate 0–3 record with the Low grade handed over as a prior finding rather than a verdict, so no late Gate 4 is owed.]
Significance — consequence: Weak. A non-zero static-coordinate term would make shelf position a quality attribute — stratified release testing, position-aware allocation of high-value units, position as a retrospective covariate, a new entry in ISBER/FACT-NetCord/AABB storage guidance. A null licenses current practice with evidence. Either answer is partly pre-empted by Prior 1's null on the larger insult.
Significance — audience: Real but not shown to act. ART laboratory directors, cord-blood and cell-therapy QA, biorepository operations, standards bodies. Vendors own the measurement side with a commercial incentive and have published uniformity data for years without attaching an outcome. Nothing in 20 queries shows any standards body treating intra-vessel position as a quality attribute.
Significance — fecundity: Thin, with one live item: whether reported cryostorage-*duration* effects are partly position effects in disguise, since sequential tank filling confounds position with date. That derivative is not foreclosed by Prior 1 and is more significant than the candidate as framed; it should be intaken as its own candidate. A null here adds little that Prior 1's null does not.
Significance — anchoring: The unresolved cryostorage-duration literature (where position–date confounding is an unexamined alternative explanation), the vapour- versus liquid-phase storage debate, the unexplained between-centre spread in post-thaw survival, and the preanalytical-variable programme in biospecimen science (SPREC and successors), which codes storage temperature but not position.
Reason for silence: A conceptual-frame mechanism, evidenced rather than asserted: in regulated cold storage, intra-chamber position is constituted as a *compliance* object — map the chamber, qualify the warmest location, place worst case there — so it never becomes a research variable with an outcome attached. That explains Prior 1's silence on a coordinate it had in hand, which a funding-ownership gap does not. Compounding it: coordinate lives in operations/LIMS while the endpoint lives in clinical or QC systems, and a positive finding would be a self-reported storage-quality defect with licensing consequences. The record's third leg — a principled physical dismissal because every position sits far below Tg — is weakened, since the source invoked for it warns about vapour-phase storage and the thermometry relied on is a near-empty uniformity-marketed vessel. Evidence for the frame mechanism is guidance- and vendor-level, not primary regulation (adversary attack 7: Partial).
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): One adversary (fresh context, Gate 0–3 record only; 9 web searches, 4 fetches, 1 dead). Verbatim log: batches/2026-10-16-1433/UQ-20261016-36-adversary-1.md.
1. Triviality | A page of sub-Tg physics answers it: 10 °C at 60–70 °C below Tg is zero to within noise. | No quantitative sub-Tg rate law for the −195/−180 regime could be sourced, so the kill is unavailable at the required standard of proof; Vysekantsev et al. (2020) experimentally report extradeath on upward temperature variation from −196 °C, so the field does not treat the dose relation as flat. The requested variance share and per-10 °C effect are not derivable from anything published. | Resolved
2. Disguise | A known question in ART clothes — pharma cold-chain mapping, biobank batch-effect analysis, genebank viability monitoring, or non-English ART have asked it. | 9 new queries across 8 untried vocabularies (Chinese ART, Spanish ART/vet, genebank germplasm, cord-blood thermometry, statistical variance-component/batch-effect, transfusion −80 mapping, pharma GxP qualification, two answer-side phrasings) found no study regressing a per-unit post-thaw endpoint on static in-vessel coordinate and no variance decomposition containing a position term. GxP is the nearest structural analogue and it qualifies the warm location instead of studying outcomes by it — a different act, not the same question renamed. | Resolved

Combinatorial novelty | Thermal maps × post-thaw registries, joined because both exist; data plumbing, no problem at the interface. | A real identification problem lives there, verified in primary data: sequential filling confounds coordinate with date, and Prior 1 shows the same confound in event-count form (P < 0.001), so recovery needs the re-racking/tank-transfer instrument the candidate names. Prior 1 also proves per-unit coordinate histories are reconstructable. | Resolved

The contradiction is also over-extended: it rests on a near-empty isothermal vessel plus a CFD model, while Prior 2 per the CONICET record treats −50/−70 °C as in-dewar vapour-phase temperatures and warns that vapour-phase storage carries devitrification risk. Verification by the run session (two fresh-context checkers, one over Prior 1 and one over the standards claim behind attack 6, each handed the claim and its source but not the reviewer's reasoning; Prior 1's checker ran 14 searches and 8 fetches with 5 refusals, the standards checker 14 and 6 with 7; full logs in batches/2026-10-16-1433/UQ-20261016-36-verification.md and -verification-standards.md). The novelty negative holds and is now triply sourced. Attack 6 does not hold at the standard it was graded on, and is downgraded from Unresolved to Partial.
(i) PRIOR 1 IS CONFIRMED NOT TO BE ABOUT THE CANDIDATE'S OBJECT, which is the load-bearing check. Zhang et al. 2023 estimates nothing about where a unit sat. The recorded cane/canister/tank coordinates are used ONLY as bookkeeping, to reconstruct which straws shared a cane and therefore which cane movements each straw rode along with; position is an input to building the exposure and never itself an exposure. Table 4's predictor set is EAF plus ten clinical and laboratory confounders, of which the only storage-related one is storage TIME. There is no tank-, canister-, cane-, rack- or height-level term, no random effect for location, no ICC and no variance component anywhere in the paper.
(ii) THE MECHANISM IN THE RECORD IS WRONG, and the correct one is more interesting. The record describes EAF as counting events in which a neighbouring unit was retrieved while the index unit stayed in the vessel. It does not: "the EAF of a straw was decided by the frequency of the cane contained with the straw in and out of the LN2 tank", and "the cane containing a straw was taken out from a canister in the LN2 tank into a LN2 container". The index straw is itself lifted out of the tank, into a Styrofoam LN2 container, every time its cane moves — including when the movement is for a co-located straw. The mechanism is CO-TRAVEL, not bystander exposure. The co-location element is real (up to nine straws share a cane, and "If more than one straw was taken out or put into one cane simultaneously, EAF was added as the rule of one straw"), but the exposure is a count of the index unit's own removals, which makes Prior 1 a study of handling events and leaves static position untouched — strengthening, not weakening, the novelty finding.
(iii) Prior 1's estimand is mis-stated twice in the record. EAF counts air-exposure movements in BOTH directions, out of and into the tank, and is incremented by the index embryo's own vitrification and warming, so it is not a count of other units' retrievals. And it is not modelled as a count at all: it enters as a five-level CATEGORICAL variable (2 / 4 / 6 / 8 / >=10) with EAF = 2 as reference, reported as four category contrasts plus an overall P per embryo-day block, with no per-event slope, no dose-response test and no trend statistic. The authors state the limitation themselves, verbatim: "The third limitation is that EAF is calculated by the number of exposed-to-air during the procedure rather than duration time of exposed-to-air."
(iv) The headline null checks out and must be carried with its own uncertainty. D3, EAF >= 10, clinical pregnancy: adjusted OR 0.867 (95% CI 0.672-1.119, P = 0.274), relative to EAF = 2, in the 3,313-cycle day-3 subgroup, inside a block whose overall EAF P = 0.232. The interval is log-symmetric about the estimate (implied SE 0.1301, z = -1.096, recomputed two-sided p = 0.273 against the printed 0.274) and spans 1: compatible with anything from 33% lower to 12% higher odds. The companion live-birth value is 0.898 (0.688-1.173, P = 0.431). The stratum counts sum exactly (3,313 + 4,530 + 1,357 = 9,200). Two smaller corrections: post-warming survival is DEFINED in Methods and reported descriptively in Tables 1-3 but is not an endpoint of the adjusted regression, so there is no adjusted estimate for it; and EAF = 2's status as reference is printed in Table 4, not stated in any prose sentence.
(v) THE NOVELTY NEGATIVE IS INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED A THIRD TIME. Thirteen further searches for any study, in any cryostorage field, estimating an association or variance component between a unit's static in-vessel position and a per-unit post-thaw outcome returned NOT FOUND. Everything that came back fell into an excluded bucket: storage duration, storage phase or temperature, transient warming during retrieval (where Prior 1 itself sits), chamber thermal uniformity with no outcome attached, and hardware design comparisons. Gate 2 found this, the adversary's nine Disguise queries in eight untried vocabularies reproduced it, and this is the third independent context to return it.
(vi) ATTACK 6 IS DOWNGRADED TO PARTIAL, on two grounds. First, its exhaustive negative cannot be supported by what was actually read: of nine document families named, four were never opened (AABB, ISO 20387, ISO 21973/24190, the GMP annexes, SPREC), and of those opened, the storage clauses sat outside the readable text in three (FACT-JACIE C10/D9, NetCord-FACT D6/D7, HFEA GN 17); the only free ISBER full text reachable was the THIRD EDITION of 2012, and that read stopped around section D3, before the Biological Material Tracking section whose own contents line reads "I2.100 Specimen Location". The honest form of the claim is narrower than "nothing shows". Second, the objection's central leg is mis-sourced: ISBER C8.000 does not say to place worst-case material at the warmest point. What it says is that "different locations in the equipment might exhibit different temperatures depending on the size and age of the unit" and that mapping is done "so that warm and cold spots that could be problematic for material storage can be identified". The existing-control argument was the reason attack 6 was graded fatal-adjacent, and the document it was attributed to does not make it.
(vii) The one genuine refutation runs the other way, and it helps the candidate. NetCord-FACT Cord Blood Standards 8th edition B9.2.4 requires "Location within the storage device" and B9.2.3 a "Storage device identifier" as inventory fields held against the unit. So the candidate's exposure variable is already recorded at unit level in accredited cord-blood banks — a feasibility finding, not a significance one, since recording a location for retrieval is category (a) and says nothing about treating it as a quality attribute. No documented instance of any facility, regulator or accreditation body using in-vessel position as a decision input in an investigation, deviation, recall or release decision was found.
(viii) The strongest near-miss in the standards, which the batch did not find: NetCord-FACT A4 defines a "Representative sample" as an "Aliquot of the final cord blood product that is stored under the same conditions as the cord blood unit." That is the natural place for a standard to require co-location or matched position, and in the readable text it requires matched CONDITIONS only. A standard that governs the one aliquot whose job is to stand in for the unit, and does not require it to sit in the same place, is a sharper statement of the candidate's gap than anything in the Gate 2 record.
(ix) Fidelity caveat on both checks: every quotation came through a fetch tool whose extraction layer caps verbatim strings at about 125 characters, and raw HTTP to all five standards hosts was refused by the proxy (403). Several standards quotes are sentence fragments rather than whole clauses, and on Prior 1 one long Methods sentence — whether a neighbour-only warming increments the index straw's EAF — could not be retrieved contiguously; the cane-level definition implies it does, and the checker flagged that as an inference from two short fragments rather than a single quoted sentence.

Gate 4 completeness after verification: complete for the purpose of this verdict, and no late adversary is required. No fatal ground fell — attack 6 is not in the fatal set — so the sequential rule's second adversary remains a promotion condition rather than a correction owed.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 1/3
Strongest remaining objection: The answer has no one who would act on it — attack 6, now Partial rather than Unresolved, and still the binding objection. What survives verification is the part that was never about the standards: the vendors who own the measurement have published uniformity data for years without attaching an outcome; no facility, regulator or accreditation body was found using in-vessel position as a decision input in any investigation, deviation, recall or release decision; and the single facility verified to hold coordinate-linked outcomes tested the larger thermal insult across 9,200 cycles and reported a null, which makes a smaller sub-Tg static effect both hard to credit and uninteresting to act on even if estimated. What does not survive is the claim that an institutional control already handles it — that was attributed to ISBER, which does not say it. So the objection is now an absence of demonstrated demand rather than the presence of a substitute, which is weaker but still enough to hold Significance at 1/3 and the verdict at Provisional.
Promotion requires: (1) attack 6 resolved with evidence rather than speculation — a named facility, accreditation body or standard documented as willing to treat a position variance component or a per-10 °C effect size as a decision input, lifting Significance to at least 2/3; and because verification showed the batch's negative was not exhaustive, this now specifically requires reading what was not read: the CURRENT ISBER Best Practices (not the 2012 third edition) including its Biological Material Tracking section, AABB Standards for Cellular Therapy Services, ISO 20387, ISO 21973/24190, EU GMP Annexes 1 and 2, SPREC, and the storage clauses of FACT-JACIE C10/D9, NetCord-FACT D6/D7 and HFEA GN 17, all of which sat outside the readable text. The near-miss at NetCord-FACT A4 — a representative sample must be stored under the same CONDITIONS, not in the same place — is the sharpest place to start; (2) attack 5 closed by a design that states how a single-site estimate becomes a transferable claim about vapour-phase storage, and presupposition 2 settled from the full Theriogenology text of Prior 2 plus position-resolved thermometry in a loaded, routinely opened conventional dewar, lifting Well-posedness to 3/3; (3) the second adversary that the sequential rule skipped run on the Gate 0–3 record, returning nothing Unresolved on attacks 1, 2 or 4. Promotion also requires the revised Medium novelty grade to survive that second adversary's own Disguise sweep.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Re-open Prior 1's dataset at the facility that holds it: Zhang et al. report logging cane, canister and tank position for all 9,200 cycles and leaving the coordinate unanalysed. A coordinate-stratified reanalysis of that existing extract with the facility's own vessel thermal map attached is cheaper than instrumenting a new facility.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed — not rejected, and not asked-and-open. Prior 1 answered a different estimand, so the surviving question is neither answered nor an open problem of record. The derivative worth carrying forward — whether published cryostorage-duration effects are confounded with storage position by sequential tank filling — should be intaken as a fresh candidate, not routed.

ID: UQ-20261016-37
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): STEM/medicine — sterilization science and microbial inactivation kinetics; pharmaceutical/device regulatory science. Adjacent vocabularies: food thermal processing (12D cook, Weibull), reliability demonstration testing, nuclear PRA.
Question (canonical): For terminally sterilized products certified at a PNSU/SAL of 10^-6, over a fixed window with an enumerated released-unit denominator: (i) what one-sided lower bound on the realized probability of intrinsic non-sterility per released unit does the ascertained record (release sterility-test failures, non-sterility recalls, confirmed intrinsic-contamination outbreaks) support, under an explicit attribution rule and a stated ascertainment interval; and (ii) if that bound exceeds 10^-6, is the excess reproduced in direction and order of magnitude by recomputing PNSU for the same cycles under published non-log-linear (shoulder/tailing, Weibull) parameters? (V1, Gate 1 reformulation of the intake V0 frequency-claim version; both in the record.)
Alternative formulations: Does the realized non-sterility rate of terminally sterilized product match the one-in-a-million that licensed its release, and has anyone done that arithmetic? / What interval on the true probability of a non-sterile unit does the observed population of sterility failures support, versus the extrapolated SAL used at release?
Motivating gap: Presupposition inversion. Release rests on a probability extrapolated ~6 logs below the smallest measurable survivor endpoint (BIs carry ~10^6 spores: 2-3 demonstrable logs against a 12-log claim), and the one available check — the extrapolated number against the realized record of a ~10^10-10^11-unit annual fleet — was assumed never attempted. Gate 2 found the epistemic limb is itself prior art.
Presuppositions: (1) SAL is a frequency statement about released units — contested at intake and fatal if false; adversary VERIFIED it survives, P1 defines SAL as "not more than one viable microorganism in one million sterilized items", so the record's weakening of this presupposition is struck as overstated. (2) The 10^-6-certified annual fleet is enumerable to an order of magnitude — partially supported (industry/National Academies EtO figures, tens of billions US devices/yr; not opened). (3) Ascertainment fraction boundable — contested; the field's own position is that it is not. (4) Events attributable to terminal-sterilization failure — UNRESOLVED in the record and the point on which Gate 4 kills the candidate. (5) Non-log-linear parameters exist for the relevant cycle/organism/carrier combinations — unestablished. (6) Frame restricted to 10^-6-certified product (some categories at 10^-3) — supported. (7) Release sterility testing has characterised sensitivity — contested; FDA 2004 via adversary source C: the test detects contamination only in lots with ~>=10% units contaminated.
What would count as an answer: (a) enumerated 10^-6-certified released-unit denominator with a range; (b) ascertained numerator of confirmed intrinsic non-sterility with ascertainment interval and an attribution rule excluding aseptic fill, post-sterilization container-closure breach and in-use contamination; (c) the resulting one-sided interval on the realized rate; (d) PNSU recomputed for the same cycles under published tail-aware parameters. Answered one way if the interval excludes 10^-6 and (d) reproduces the gap's sign and magnitude; the other way if it contains 10^-6 and (d) stays at or below it. One-sided by construction.
Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 11 of 11 budgeted (full list: batches/2026-10-16-1433/UQ-20261016-37-record.md). Most informative: ["sterility assurance level" is not a real probability criticism unfalsifiable 10-6] -> von Woedtke & Kramer 2008 (publisso) + Manufacturing Chemist "Balance of probabilities" — decisive. [Agalloco Akers "myth of sterility assurance" PNSU 10-6 meaningless number sterilization] (mandatory own-field title query) -> PharmTech "The Myth Called 'Sterility'"; PDA J 73(6):615; PubMed 2277313 (1990, not opened). [how many billion sterile medical devices ... annual terminal sterilization volume] (mandatory quantity query) -> denominator already published at order of magnitude (tens of billions US EtO devices/yr); numerator-as-a-rate not. [probabilistic risk assessment predicted failure frequency versus observed operating experience] -> the transplanted METHOD is mature and named in nuclear PRA (arXiv:1405.6658, NRC/PNNL). [12D botulinum cook ... realized failure rate] -> recorded as a negative; CONTRADICTED by adversary source A. Plus 9 adversary Disguise queries in German, French, canning, radiation-dose-audit, recall-enforcement, epidemiology, Bayesian and hospital-reprocessing vocabularies (UQ-20261016-37-adversary-1.md).
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): P1 von Woedtke T, Kramer A, "The limits of sterility assurance," GMS Hyg Infect Control 3(1):Doc19, 2008, https://journals.publisso.de/en/journals/hic/volume3/dgkh000117 — unit: sterilization processes/product categories; endpoint: whether 10^-6 is experimentally provable, plus a normative 10^-6/10^-4/10^-3 tiering; comparator: highest experimentally accessible level (~10^-2) against the required 10^-6, and asserted infection rates at 10^-6 vs 10^-3; estimand: none (argumentative/normative). Opened by both record and adversary; quotes match. P2 Akers JE, Agalloco JP, "The Myth Called 'Sterility'," Pharmaceutical Technology, Mar 2010, https://www.pharmtech.com/view/myth-called-sterility — unit: aseptic processes and their monitoring instruments; endpoint: provability of sterility from monitoring evidence; comparator: assay detection limits; estimand: none; SAL/PNSU not mentioned. Not re-verified by the adversary (budget). P3 "Balance of probabilities," Manufacturing Chemist, 30 Apr 2002, https://manufacturingchemist.com/balance-of-probabilities-31246 — unit: items within a sterilized batch/irradiation load; endpoint: SAL as design and validation target (EN 556 10^-6; US non-invasive 10^-3); estimand: the extrapolated survivor probability itself, stated uncritically, no field data.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — it does not differ as a question. P1 poses the provability question in the candidate's own field and nearly its own words, answers it (not evidence-based, not experimentally ascertainable), attributes the failure to non-exponential/tailing kinetics, and pre-emptively dismisses the field-outcome comparison as impracticable (citing Winckels & Dorpema 1994). The candidate supplies only deliverables (a)-(d), i.e. the undone method inside an already-posed question. vs P2 — different object (aseptic, not terminal) and endpoint; prior art only for "sterility claims are not directly verifiable". vs P3 — same estimand, but P3 states the convention rather than testing it; weak trade-press prior art. Method-owning-field negative must be stated narrowly: comparing an extrapolated low-probability failure claim against an operating fleet's record is routine in nuclear PRA and reliability demonstration testing; the only defensible negative is that nobody has run it on the sterilization SAL. Adversary further narrowed this: the arithmetic HAS been published in the sister field (source A: NFPA/CMI Container Integrity Task Force, 1.3x10^12 cans 1940-82, 5 leakage-attributed botulinal incidents, 3.8x10^-12 realized, set beside Odlaug & Pflug's modelled 10^-7-10^-10), and radiation sterilization runs a realized positive-fraction check via ISO 11137/ISO 13004 dose audits at SAL 10^-2.
Novelty confidence: Low
Significance — consequence: If the realized interval excluded 10^-6 and the tail-aware recomputation reproduced the gap, parametric release and the overkill basis of ISO 11135/11137/17665 and USP <1222>/Ph.Eur. 5.1.1 would need a tail-aware PNSU — a change to the arithmetic of release. If it contained 10^-6, the convention is vindicated as a conservative bound and P1's standing proposal to relax whole classes to 10^-4/10^-3 loses practical force. Limited by asymmetry: the numerator is an undercount by construction, so the null is weak — and per Gate 4 the achievable result is that uninformative direction.
Significance — audience: ISO/TC 198 and the AAMI sterilization working groups, USP <1211>/<1222> and Ph.Eur. 5.1.1 expert committees, notified bodies and FDA CDRH/CDER reviewers granting parametric release, hospital infection control. Deflated at Gate 4: the pending decision has already been taken without this arithmetic — ISO/TS 19930 provides a risk-based route to SALs other than 10^-6 for product that cannot withstand 10^-6 processing (BSI listing, title only, not opened).
Significance — fecundity: Makes askable (i) what the ascertainment fraction for intrinsic non-sterility is and what surveillance design would make SAL falsifiable at all; (ii) what conservatism 12 logs buys over 6 in cost, product damage and foregone low-temperature modalities; (iii) the general form for any certified-but-unobservable probability (aviation 10^-9/h budgets, PRA core-damage frequency).
Significance — anchoring: mechanistic-vs-vitalistic survivor-curve dispute; EMA Annex 1 physical-vs-biological evidence dispute (Agalloco 2019, "The Bugs Don't Lie"); P1's unadopted tiered-SAL proposal; validation of extrapolated low-probability claims against operating experience in nuclear PRA and RDT.
Reason for silence: Split custody (manufacturers/contract sterilizers hold the denominator and have no incentive to falsify their own release basis; recall and outbreak surveillance holds the numerator and is organised by product and hazard, not sterilization modality) plus an authoritative foreclosure — P1 declared the field-outcome comparison practically impossible, converting an open empirical question into a closed rhetorical one. Adversary's better mechanism, accepted: practitioners judged the comparison uninformative rather than merely impractical, because recalls measure quality-system failure and not the kinetic tail. Either way the silence is partial and the question was asked (Winckels & Dorpema 1994; von Woedtke & Kramer 2008).
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): one adversary ran (Gate 4 sequential rule; the second was not needed because the fatal ground held on verification). Disguise VERIFIED: 9 new-vocabulary queries run against the >=8 requirement, 4 pages opened. Verbatim log: UQ-20261016-37-adversary-1.md.

Verification by the run session (one fresh-context checker over P1 and the canning arithmetic, handed the claims and their sources but not the reviewer's reasoning; 10 searches, 6 fetches, 8 refusals or blocks; full log in batches/2026-10-16-1433/UQ-20261016-37-verification.md). The verdict stands on Gate 4. Two of the Gate 2 record's three characterisations of P1 are wrong, and the one the record called decisive is wrong in its central assertion.
(i) CLAIM REFUTED, and it was the record's load-bearing reading of P1. P1 does NOT pre-emptively dismiss, as impracticable, the comparison of the claimed SAL against the field record of sterile products. The sentence citing Winckels & Dorpema [85] says it is practically impossible to find a difference in the RATE OF INFECTION between products sterilized to an SAL of 10^-6 and products from a procedure ensuring only a 10^-3 contamination likelihood. That is a between-TIER discrimination argument, and P1 deploys it to justify RELAXING the required SAL, not to close off the realized-record comparison. The record read an argument for lowering the bar as a refusal to measure against it.
(ii) P1 does not POSE the provability question; it ASSERTS the answer. A request for an interrogative sentence about provability returned nothing on the page. The only question P1 poses is its section heading, "Do the current theoretical sterility assurance requirements reflect the actual safety requirements?" The assertion itself is confirmed and is stronger than the record states, with three limbs rather than two: the SAL is "neither evidence based nor can it be accurately ascertained in experiments, or attained practically".
(iii) The attribution to tailing kinetics is over-stated. P1 gives TWO independent grounds for unprovability: a generic limit of detection of about "10-2 test organisms per test object", which holds whatever the kinetics, and non-linear or tailing survivor curves, which it argues specifically for non-thermal and low-temperature processes rather than universally — the authors conclude that only steam and dry heat are properly validated. The 10^-2 figure is an expected-count limit of detection per test object, not a bare probability, and should not be quoted without its units. P1 also proposes a FOURTH, non-numeric tier the record omits: "microbiologically safe for the designated use".
(iv) The record's own adjacent-field claim needed four corrections. The canning figures are real but: 1.3 x 10^12 cans of low-acid food were CONSUMED, not produced, and the figure is not restricted to the United States; 3.8 x 10^-12 is a probability of botulism per can consumed, which the task force presents as a risk estimate ("one chance in every 260 billion cans of foods consumed") rather than self-describing it as a realized rate, though it is numerically the observed incidents-per-can ratio; the arithmetic checks (5 / 1.3e12 = 3.85e-12); and the Odlaug & Pflug 10^-7 to 10^-10 range is the likelihood of POST-PROCESSING CONTAMINATION with C. botulinum, not a spoilage or survival probability — the commensurable onward estimate is 10^-9 to 10^-12, inside which 3.8e-12 sits, while it falls about 26-fold BELOW 10^-10 and so outside the range the record set it beside. "Has been set beside" is itself unsupported: Podolak 2010 presents both figures in sequence in one Introduction paragraph and never states that they agree, differ or reconcile. All of it was verified only in that secondary source (Food Protection Trends, p. 161/167); the primary NFPA/CMI paper (J Food Prot 47:801-816) was never opened, and Podolak's own reference for it is internally inconsistent on year.
(v) ONE RECORD CLAIM IS NOT CHECKED AND MUST NOT BE READ AS CHECKED. ISO 11137 and ISO 13004 are paywalled and were never opened, so nothing about what a dose audit requires is verified here, including the attachment to a sterility assurance level of 10^-2. The one secondary page read documents a "<=2 positives" acceptance rule and describes the audit as confirming the continued validity of the established dose, and mentions no SAL. The record's sentence asserting that radiation sterilization "runs a realized positive-fraction check via ISO 11137/ISO 13004 dose audits at SAL 10^-2" is therefore downgraded to unverified — not refuted, not confirmed.
(vi) Quotation-fidelity caveat that binds every quote above, including (i). No raw copy of P1 was obtainable — all direct transport was proxy-denied — and the only available reader caps each quoted string at about 125 characters and refused three requests for longer text. So no sentence longer than that cap exists in verbatim form in this check, the decisive claim-(i) sentence included; it is reported as the reader returned it.
(vii) What none of this changes. The verdict does not rest on the struck readings. P1 still asserts, in the candidate's own literature and nearly its own words, the answer to the candidate's epistemic question, which is enough for Low at Gate 2; and the rejection is independently carried by Gate 4, where attack 4 is Unresolved and fatal under the Gate 4 rule. What the corrections do change is the routing decision below.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: The numerator the question specifies can only ever be populated by gross lot-level process failures — a release sterility test cannot see below ~10% lot contamination — whereas a 10^-6 kinetic-tail survivor is a single unit in a correctly processed lot that generates no detectable event. So even a realized bound above 10^-6 could not be attributed to the log-linear extrapolation: limb (ii) is unidentifiable from the data limb (i) collects. Unresolved (attack 4, fatal), independently of the Gate 2 finding.
Verdict reasoning (Gate 5), as amended after verification: Rejected, and the decisive ground is now GATE 4 rather than Gate 2. Attack 4 (Presupposition failure) is Unresolved and fatal under the Gate 4 rule: a 10^-6 kinetic-tail survivor is by construction a lone unit in an otherwise correctly processed lot, so it produces no lot-level signal and fails no release sterility test, and the realized record cannot bear on the kinetic extrapolation at all. Attack 8 is Unresolved with it. Gate 2's Low also survives, but narrowed — P1 asserts rather than poses the epistemic answer, and the "pre-emptive dismissal" the record built on is a between-tier argument for relaxing the SAL, not a refusal to measure against the field record (see Verification (i)-(iii)). Well-posedness is independently 2/3. Original Gate 2 reasoning, retained for the record: P1 is an on-point peer-reviewed paper in the candidate's own literature and nearly its own words that poses and answers the epistemic question, attributes the failure to tailing kinetics, and dismisses the field-outcome comparison; the candidate supplies only the undone arithmetic inside an already-posed question, which is asked-but-open, not un-asked. Confirmed at Gate 4: Unresolved on attack 4 (fatal under the Gate 4 rule) and on attack 8. Also independently short of Validated on Well-posedness 2/3. Two record claims are struck on verification by the adversary: the weakening of presupposition 1 (P1 does define SAL as a frequency) and the query-11 adjacent-field negative (the canning realized-record arithmetic exists). Neither strike removes a kill, so no second adversary was required.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Settle identifiability before any arithmetic — ask whether any existing or designable surveillance stream can distinguish a single-unit kinetic-tail survivor from a gross lot-level process failure; and open the unexamined leads first (Winckels & Dorpema 1994 "Risk assessment as a basis for the definition of sterility"; PubMed 2277313, 1990; ISO/TS 19930; ISO 11137-2 dose-setting).
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): NOT ROUTED. The batch proposed a row and the run session withdrew it; no row was appended, and this line is the record of why.
  The ledger's own Gate 4 squeezes the question from both sides. Attack 8 splits it into a gross process-failure rate, which recall surveillance already tracks and which is unrelated to survivor-curve shape, and a kinetic-tail probability, which attack 4 shows is unobservable by construction — no lot-level signal, no failed sterility test. So the tractable limb is already measured by someone else and the open limb is not identifiable from the data the question names. Routing it would hand the research run a quantity its own ledger has shown cannot be estimated, which is exactly the harm the routing test exists to prevent.
  The posed-in-print test is also weaker than the batch thought. P1's only interrogative is a section heading, it asserts rather than defers the empirical answer, and the sentence the record took for a deferral turns out to be an argument for lowering the required SAL (Verification (i)-(ii)). The canning precedent — a realized per-can rate computed over a fleet and set beside modelled probabilities — is a genuine transplant target, but no paper poses it for medical-device sterilization, and a quantity nobody has asked for is not an open problem (routing rule (a)).
  Kept here rather than in the routing file so a later run does not re-derive it: the only defensible residual is a weak one-sided bound at ascertainment = 1, and it belongs in a fresh Gate 0 intake with the non-identifiability carried as a condition of admission.
